metadata.title: Primes with a missing digit: distribution in arithmetic progressions and an application in sieve theory

extraction_notes.note: The two dependency diagrams in 'Organization of the paper' are replaced by placeholders in the source; nothing extracted from them.
Section 9 lemmas are marked external (Maynard's Lemmas 5.1-5.4, 'collected from Maynard') although the paper adapts them to A_r via a factorisation; they could be read as paper results.
The Section 2 outline of Theorem 1 is split into two proof-sketch nodes around the minor-arcs definition, so that the definition stays a top-level node.
Expected equidistribution statements in the introduction typed conjecture rather than open_problem: they are stated as estimates the author expects but cannot prove.

Generic notation items (O/<< conventions, letters for primes, gcd/lcm and interval conventions, Euler-Mascheroni gamma) and short justifying sentences of the lower-bound sieve set-up were not made nodes.

In the proof of Theorem 1 the claim opener 'Now we check the three conditions' is followed by a paragraph break (rule 7 would close it at once); the three condition checks were nested under it as children anyway.

nodes.name: Integers with a missing digit $\mathcal{A}$
nodes.statement: Let $b\geq 3$ be an integer and let $a_0\in\{0, 1, \dotsc, b-1\}$. Consider \[\mathcal{A}:=\bigg\{\sum_{j\geq 0}n_jb^j: n_j\in \{0, \dotsc, b-1\}\setminus \{a_0\}\: \text{for all $j$}\bigg\},\] the set of non-negative integers without the digit $a_0$ in their $b$-adic expansion.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{A}$ is the set of non-negative integers with no digit $a_0$ in base $b$.
differentia: without the digit $a_0$ in their $b$-adic expansion
also_stated_at: Throughout, we fix a choice of an integer $b\geq 3$ and $a_0\in\{0,1,\dotsc,b-1\}$, and we set \[\mathcal{A}:=\bigg\{\sum_{j\geq 0}n_jb^j: n_j\in \{0, \dotsc, b-1\}\setminus \{a_0\}\: \forall j \bigg\}.\]

nodes.name: Scale $X=b^k$ and density exponent $\zeta$
nodes.statement: For the rest of the paper, we set $X=b^k$ and note that there are $\approx X^{\zeta}$ elements in $\mathcal{A}$ less than $X$, where \[\zeta :=\frac{\log(b-1)}{\log b}<1.\]
nodes.statement_short: Set $X=b^k$; $\mathcal{A}$ has about $X^\zeta$ elements below $X$, with $\zeta=\log(b-1)/\log b<1$.
also_stated_at: We set $X=b^k$ with $k\in \mathbb{N}$ and $k\rightarrow \infty$ for the rest of the paper except Part \ref{part: exp sum}.
Furthermore, we set $\zeta := \frac{\log (b-1)}{\log b}$ for the rest of the paper.

nodes.name: $\zeta\to 1$ as $b\to\infty$
nodes.statement: Note that $\zeta \rightarrow 1$ as $b\rightarrow \infty$. We shall have many occasions to use this fact in the paper, and we do so without further comment.

nodes.name: Expected equidistribution of missing-digit primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.statement: For $(c, d)=1$ and $(d,b)=1$, one expects that as $X\to \infty$, \begin{align} \notag \#\{p<X:p\equiv c\imod d, p\in \mathcal{A}\} \sim \dfrac{1}{\varphi(d)}\#\{p<X:p\in \mathcal{A}\} \end{align} holds uniformly for $d\leq X^{\zeta(1-\varepsilon)}$ with any fixed $\varepsilon>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Primes in $\mathcal{A}$ should be equidistributed in reduced classes mod $d$ for $d\le X^{\zeta(1-\varepsilon)}$.
assumptions: uniformly for $d\leq X^{\zeta(1-\varepsilon)}$ with any fixed $\varepsilon>0$

nodes.name: Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem for primes with a missing digit at level $X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$
nodes.statement: Instead, we aim for a Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem of the following type: \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c, d)=1}\bigg|\#\{p<X:p\equiv c\imod d, p\in \mathcal{A}\} - \dfrac{1}{\varphi(d)}\#\{p<X:p\in \mathcal{A}\}\bigg| \ll_{A,b} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A}, \end{align} where $D\leq X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, provided that $b$ is large enough in terms of $\varepsilon$ (so that $\zeta$ is close enough to $1$).
nodes.statement_short: A Bombieri-Vinogradov bound for primes in $\mathcal{A}$ with moduli up to $X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$, for $b$ large; not proved here.

nodes.name: von Mangoldt function
nodes.statement: For technical convenience, we will work with the von Mangoldt function $\Lambda$ (recall that $\Lambda(n)=\log p$ if $n=p^m$, and $0$ otherwise).

nodes.name: Error term $\mathcal{E}(X; d, c; b, r)$
nodes.statement: For $X=b^k$ with $k\in \mathbb{N}$ and for $(c, d)=(r, b)=1$, we set \begin{align} \notag \mathcal{E}(X; d, c; b, r):=\sum_{\substack{n < X\\n\equiv c \imod d\\n\equiv r\imod b}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}}(n) - \dfrac{1}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(n). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{E}$ is the discrepancy between $\Lambda 1_{\mathcal{A}}$ in a progression mod $d$ and last digit $r$, and its expected share.
also_stated_at: For $(c,d)=(r,b)=1$, we set \begin{align} \notag \mathcal{E}(X;d,c;b,r)=\sum_{\substack{n < X\\n\equiv c \imod d\\n\equiv r\imod b}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}}(n) - \dfrac{1}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(n). \end{align}

nodes.name: Count of $\mathcal{A}$ below $X$ with a given last digit
nodes.statement: Note that \[\sum_{\substack{n<X\\ n\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(n) = \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{b-1}\] whenever $r\not\equiv a_0\imod b$; otherwise, both sums in the definition of $\mathcal{E}(X; d, c;b,r)$ is $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Exactly $X^\zeta/(b-1)$ elements of $\mathcal{A}$ below $X$ have last digit $r\ne a_0$.

nodes.name: Bombieri-Vinogradov type theorem for primes with a missing digit
nodes.statement: Let $\delta>0$ and let $b$ be an integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$. Let $D\in [1, X^{1/3-\delta}]$ and let $r\in \mathcal{A}\cap[0, b)$ be an integer such that $(r, b)=1$. Then for any $A>0$, we have \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\big|\mathcal{E}(X;d,c;b,r)\big| \ll_{A, b, \delta} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: For large base $b$, primes with a missing digit are equidistributed on average over moduli $d\le X^{1/3-\delta}$.
assumptions: $b$ be an integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$
$r\in \mathcal{A}\cap[0, b)$ be an integer such that $(r, b)=1$
nodes.label: Main Theorem

nodes.name: Equation (1.1)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\big|\mathcal{E}(X;d,c;b,r)\big| \ll_{A, b, \delta} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A}.
nodes.label: MT1eq1

nodes.name: Bombieri-Vinogradov type theorem with composite moduli $d_1d_2$
nodes.statement: Let $\delta>0$, let $b$ be an integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$, and let \[D_1\in [1, X^{1/3-\delta}] \quad \text{and} \quad D_2\in [1, X^{1/9}].\] Let $c$ be a non-zero integer and let $r\in \mathcal{A}\cap[0, b)$ with $(r, b)=1$. Then for any $A>0$, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{d_1\leq D_1}} \sideset{}{^*}\sum_{\substack{d_2\leq D_2}}\big|\mathcal{E}(X; d_1d_2, c; b, r)\big| \ll_{A, b, \delta} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A}, \end{align} where $^*$ in the sum denotes the conditions $(c,d_1d_2)=(b,d_1d_2)=(d_1, d_2)=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Same equidistribution with a fixed residue $c$ over composite moduli $d_1d_2$, $d_1\le X^{1/3-\delta}$, $d_2\le X^{1/9}$.
assumptions: $b$ be an integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$
conclusions: \sum_{\substack{d_1\leq D_1}} \sideset{}{^*}\sum_{\substack{d_2\leq D_2}}\big|\mathcal{E}(X; d_1d_2, c; b, r)\big| \ll_{A, b, \delta} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A},
nodes.label: Main Theorem2

nodes.name: Well-factorable function
nodes.statement: Let $D\geq 1$ be a real number. We say an arithmetic function $\xi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ \emph{well-factorable} of level $D$ if, for any choice of factorization $D = D_1D_2$ with $D_1, D_2 \geq 1$, there exist two arithmetic functions $\xi_1, \xi_2:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ such that \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $|\xi_1|, |\xi_2|\leq 1$. \item $\xi_1$ is supported on $[1, D_1]$ and $\xi_2$ is supported on $[1, D_2]$. \item We have\footnote{In general, we do not require the co-primality condition in the definition of $\xi$. However, in order to avoid some technical issues, we impose this condition here.} \[\xi(d)=\sum_{\substack{d_1d_2=d\\(d_1, d_2)=1}}\xi_1(d_1)\xi_2(d_2).\] \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $\xi$ is well-factorable of level $D$ if for every $D=D_1D_2$ it is a coprime convolution of bounded $\xi_1,\xi_2$ supported up to $D_1,D_2$.
nodes.label: def: well fac

nodes.name: Bombieri-Vinogradov type theorem with well-factorable weights
nodes.statement: Let $\delta>0$ and let $b$ be an integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$. Let $\xi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be a well-factorable arithmetic function of level $D\in [1, X^{1/2-\delta}]$. Let $c$ be a non-zero integer and let $r\in \mathcal{A}\cap[0,b)$ be such that $(r, b)=1$. Then, for any $A>0$, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\ (d,bc)=1}}\xi(d)\mathcal{E}(X; d, c; b, r) \ll_{A,b,\delta}\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: With well-factorable weights of level $D\le X^{1/2-\delta}$, the weighted sum of $\mathcal{E}$ is $\ll X^\zeta/(\log X)^A$.
assumptions: $b$ be an integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$
$\xi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be a well-factorable arithmetic function of level $D\in [1, X^{1/2-\delta}]$
conclusions: \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\ (d,bc)=1}}\xi(d)\mathcal{E}(X; d, c; b, r) \ll_{A,b,\delta}\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A}.
nodes.label: Main Theorem3

nodes.name: Size of the base $b$
nodes.statement: We have not explicitly mentioned in the above three theorems the size of $b$. In fact, it will be evident from the proof that $\delta$ and $b$ are \emph{inversely related} to each other. A simple calculation suggests that the size of $b$ is approximately of order $10^{632}$ if we take $\delta=1/100$. Therefore, we will refrain from explicitly calculating $\delta$ and $b$ in the above three theorems.

nodes.name: Primes $p=1+m^2+n^2$ with a missing digit
nodes.statement: Let $b$ be an odd integer that is sufficiently large, and let \[\mathbb{B}=\{n:n=n_1^2+n_2^2~~\text{for some}~(n_1, n_2)=1\}.\] Let $r\in \mathcal{A}\cap[0, b)$ with $\big(r(r-1), b\big)=1$. Then, we have \begin{equation} \notag \sum_{\substack{p < X\\p\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(p)1_{\mathbb{B}}(p-1)\asymp_{b} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{3/2}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For large odd $b$, the number of primes $p<X$ in $\mathcal{A}$ with $p-1$ a sum of two coprime squares is $\asymp X^\zeta/(\log X)^{3/2}$.
assumptions: $b$ be an odd integer that is sufficiently large
nodes.label: Main TheoremApp

nodes.name: Strategy for the upper and lower bounds in Theorem 4
nodes.statement: The implicit upper bound in Theorem \ref{Main TheoremApp} follows from Theorem \ref{Main Theorem} and a standard upper bound sieve estimate (for example, see Lemma \ref{fundsemi}). However, for the lower bound, we need to be more careful and use an argument due to Iwaniec \cite{iwa, iwa2} that allows sieving for primes of the form $1+m^2+n^2$ using \emph{level of distribution} slightly less than $X^{1/2}$. Additionally, in order to use the sieve estimates efficiently, we need two technical results, namely, Theorem \ref{Hyp1} and Theorem \ref{Hyp2} (similar in nature to Theorems \ref{Main Theorem2}, \ref{Main Theorem3}).
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound of Theorem 4 follows from Theorem 1 and an upper sieve; lower bound needs Iwaniec's argument plus Theorems 5 and 6.

nodes.name: Totient, Möbius and divisor functions
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper, $\varphi$ will denote the totient function, $\mu$ the M\"{o}bius function, and $\uptau_h(n)$ the number of ways of writing $n$ as a product of $h$ natural numbers.

nodes.name: Additive character $e(y)$
nodes.statement: As it is customary, we denote $e(y)= e^{2\pi i y}$ for any real number $y$.

nodes.name: Dyadic notation $n\sim N$
nodes.statement: We write $n\sim N$ to denote $ N<n\leq 2N$.

nodes.name: Distance to the nearest integer $\|y\|$
nodes.statement: We use $\|y\|$ to denote $\min_{n\in \mathbb{Z}}|y-n|$.

nodes.name: Dirichlet character $\chi$
nodes.statement: Unless otherwise specified, $\chi$ will always denote a Dirichlet character modulo some positive integer.

nodes.name: Modular inverse $\overline{n}$
nodes.statement: For co-prime integers $m$ and $n$, we set $\overline{n}$ to denote the inverse of $n$ modulo $m$, that is, $n\overline{n}\equiv 1\imod m$.

nodes.name: Indicator function $1_{\mathcal{E}}$
nodes.statement: We let $1_\mathcal{E}$ to be the characteristic function of the set $\mathcal{E}$ (so $1_{\mathcal{E}}(x)=1$ if $x\in \mathcal{E}$, and $0$, otherwise).

nodes.name: Dirichlet convolution
nodes.statement: For any two arithmetic functions $\mathfrak{f}$ and $\mathfrak{g}$, we write $(\mathfrak{f}*\mathfrak{g})(n):= \sum_{ab=n}\mathfrak{f}(a)\mathfrak{g}(b)$ for their Dirichlet convolution.

nodes.name: $\ell^2$ norm of an arithmetic function
nodes.statement: For any arithmetic function $\mathfrak{f}:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$, we set $\lVert \mathfrak{f}\rVert_2: = \big(\sum_{n}|\mathfrak{f}(n)|^2\big)^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Truncations $F_{\leq U}$, $F_{>U}$
nodes.statement: For any arithmetic function $F$, we also set $F_{\leq U}(n):=F(n)\cdot 1_{n\leq U}$ and $F_{>U}(n):=F(n)\cdot 1_{n>U}$.

nodes.name: Sets $\mathbb{B}$ and $\mathcal{B}$
nodes.statement: We set $\mathbb{B}=\{n\in \mathbb{Z}: n=n_1^2+n_2^2~~\text{for some}~(n_1, n_2)=1\}$ and $\mathcal{B}=\{n\geq 1: p|n\Rightarrow p\equiv 1\imod 4\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbb{B}$: sums of two coprime squares; $\mathcal{B}$: integers all of whose prime factors are $1\bmod 4$.

nodes.name: Missing-digit integers with last digit $r$, $\mathcal{A}_r$
nodes.statement: In addition, given an integer $r\in \mathcal{A}\cap [0, b)$, we let \[\mathcal{A}_r=\{n\in \mathcal{A}: n\equiv r\imod b\}.\]
also_stated_at: Next, for $r\in \mathcal{A}$, we set \begin{align} \notag \mathcal{A}_r=\{n\in \mathcal{A}:n\equiv r\imod b\}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Fourier transform of $\mathcal{A}$
nodes.statement: Let $\widehat{{1}}_{\mathcal{A}}$ be the Fourier transform of the set $\mathcal{A}$ restricted to $\{1, \dotsc, X\}$ with $X=b^k$. Then, for any real number $\theta\in [0, 1)$, we have \begin{align} \widehat{{1}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\theta): =\sum_{n<X}{1}_{\mathcal{A}}(n)e(n\theta) = \prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigg(\sum_{0\leq n_j<b}{1}_{\mathcal{A}}(n_i)e(n_jb^j \theta)\bigg), \end{align} where $n=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}n_jb^j$.
nodes.statement_short: The Fourier transform of $\mathcal{A}\cap[0,X)$ factors as a product over the $k$ digits.
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof

nodes.name: Equation (2.1)
nodes.statement: \widehat{{1}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\theta): =\sum_{n<X}{1}_{\mathcal{A}}(n)e(n\theta) = \prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigg(\sum_{0\leq n_j<b}{1}_{\mathcal{A}}(n_i)e(n_jb^j \theta)\bigg),
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof
nodes.label: Afourier

nodes.name: Fourier transform of $\mathcal{A}_r$
nodes.statement: We then define \begin{align} \widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(\theta)&:=\sum_{n<X}{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)e(n\theta)\\ \notag &=e(r\theta)\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\bigg(\sum_{0\leq n_j<b}{1}_{\mathcal{A}}(n_j)e(n_jb^j \theta)\bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Fourier transform of $\mathcal{A}_r$, equal to $e(r\theta)$ times a digit product over $j\ge1$.
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof

nodes.name: Equation (2.2)
nodes.statement: \widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(\theta)&:=\sum_{n<X}{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)e(n\theta)\\ \notag &=e(r\theta)\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\bigg(\sum_{0\leq n_j<b}{1}_{\mathcal{A}}(n_j)e(n_jb^j \theta)\bigg).
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof
nodes.label: Arfourier

nodes.name: Trivial bound for $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}$
nodes.statement: Note that for $r\in \mathcal{A} \cap[0, b)$ and for any real number $\theta\in [0, 1)$, we have the trivial bound: \[\big|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(\theta)\big| \leq \dfrac{X^\zeta}{b-1} \leq X^\zeta,\] which we will often use in the paper.
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof

nodes.name: Fourier inversion for $1_{\mathcal{A}_r}$
nodes.statement: {1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n) = \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{0\leq t < X}\widehat{{1}}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\frac{-nt}{X}\bigg).
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof
nodes.label: fourinv

nodes.name: Exponential sum over primes in a progression $\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}$
nodes.statement: For $(c, d)=1$ and for any real number $\theta\in [0, 1)$, we set \begin{align} \widehat{\Lambda}_{d,\: c}(\theta)=\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c\imod {d}}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta). \end{align}

nodes.name: Fourier expansion of the prime sum with missing digits
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c\imod {d}\\n\equiv r\imod b}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}}(n) = \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{0\leq t<X}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\Lambda}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg).

nodes.name: Reduced form of Theorem 1 (main sum)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{\substack{1\leq c<d\\(c, d)=1}}\bigg|\dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{0\leq t<X}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\Lambda}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg) - \dfrac{1}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{n<X}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\bigg|\ll_{A, b, \delta}\dfrac{X^\zeta}{(\log X)^A}.

nodes.name: Major arcs $\mathfrak{M}$
nodes.statement: \noindent {\it Major arcs:} The \emph{major arcs} $\mathfrak{M}$ are those $t$'s in $[0, X)\cap \mathbb{Z}$ such that \[\bigg|\dfrac{t}{X}-\dfrac{a}{q}\bigg|\leq \dfrac{(\log X)^C}{X}\] for some $(a, q)=1$, $0\leq a<q$, $1\leq q\leq (\log X)^C$ with $C>0$ to be chosen later in terms of $A$.

nodes.name: Decomposition of the major arcs
nodes.statement_short: Split $\mathfrak{M}$ into $\mathfrak{M}_1$ ($q\nmid X$), $\mathfrak{M}_2$ ($q|X$, $\eta\ne0$) and $\mathfrak{M}_3$ ($t/X=a/q$, $q|X$).
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof

nodes.name: Equation (2.7)
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{M}=\mathfrak{M}_1\cup\mathfrak{M}_2\cup \mathfrak{M}_3,
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 1: major arcs
nodes.statement: We now briefly explain how we will estimate the sum \eqref{Mainsum} when $t$ is in one of the above-defined three sets of the \emph{major arcs}. \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item We use the $L^\infty$ bound for the Fourier transform of the set $\mathcal{A}_r$ and the trivial bound for $\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}(t/X)$ to estimate the sum \eqref{Mainsum} when $t\in \mathfrak{M}_1$. \item It turns out that when $t\in \mathfrak{M}_2$, we can use the Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem to handle the exponential sum $\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}(t/X)$ and the trivial bound for $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(t/X)$ in \eqref{Mainsum}. \item When $t\in \mathfrak{M}_3$, we get the main term in $\eqref{Mainsum}$ and the error term is again controlled by using the Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem. We note that $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(t/X)$ is large if $t$ is close to a number with few non-zero base-$b$ digits. \end{enumerate} This will establish our estimate in \eqref{Mainsum} when $t/X$ is in \emph{major arcs}.
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: $L^\infty$ bound on $\mathfrak{M}_1$, Bombieri-Vinogradov on $\mathfrak{M}_2$, main term plus Bombieri-Vinogradov on $\mathfrak{M}_3$.

nodes.name: Minor arcs $\mathfrak{m}$
nodes.statement: \noindent{\it Minor arcs:} The `\emph{minor arcs}' $\mathfrak{m}$ are those $t \in [0,X)\cap\mathbb{Z}$ such that $t\not\in\mathfrak{M}$.
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 1: minor arcs
nodes.statement: We use a $L^\infty-L^1$ bound to handle minor arcs as follows: \begin{align} \begin{split} \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c, d)=1} \bigg| \frac{1}{X}\sum_{t\in\mathfrak{m}} \widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}&\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)\bigg|\\ & \le \bigg(\sup_{t \in \mathfrak{m}}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c, d)=1}\bigg|\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}\bigg(\frac{-t}{X}\bigg)\bigg|\bigg)\sum_{t\in \mathfrak{m}}\dfrac{1}{X}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{t}{X}\bigg)\bigg|. \end{split} \end{align} As in Maynard \cite{May2}, we use a large-sieve type argument to control the $L^1$ sum of $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}$, which is shown to be small in Lemma \ref{lemd2}. Next, our goal is to save over the trivial bound on $\sum_{d\leq D}\max_{(c, d)=1}\Big\lvert\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}(t/X)\Big\rvert$ when $t \in \mathfrak{m}$ and $D$ as large as possible. We use estimates from exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions from the works of Matom\"aki \cite{Mat}, Mikawa \cite{Mik}, and Ter\"{a}v\"{a}inen \cite{Ter} to handle those sums over primes in Part \ref{part: exp sum}. Combining these $L^1$ and $L^\infty$ bounds, we will show that \begin{align} \notag \bigg(\sup_{t \in \mathfrak{m}}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c, d)=1}\bigg|\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}\bigg(\frac{-t}{X}\bigg)\bigg|\bigg)\sum_{t\in \mathfrak{m}}\dfrac{1}{X}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{t}{X}\bigg)\bigg| \ll_{A,b, \delta}\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{A}}. \end{align} This completes the rough outline of the proof of Theorem \ref{Main Theorem}.
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: $L^\infty$-$L^1$ split on the minor arcs, combining a large-sieve $L^1$ bound with exponential sums over primes in progressions.
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof

nodes.name: $L^\infty$-$L^1$ split
nodes.statement: We use a $L^\infty-L^1$ bound to handle minor arcs as follows: \begin{align} \begin{split} \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c, d)=1} \bigg| \frac{1}{X}\sum_{t\in\mathfrak{m}} \widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}&\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)\bigg|\\ & \le \bigg(\sup_{t \in \mathfrak{m}}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c, d)=1}\bigg|\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}\bigg(\frac{-t}{X}\bigg)\bigg|\bigg)\sum_{t\in \mathfrak{m}}\dfrac{1}{X}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{t}{X}\bigg)\bigg|. \end{split} \end{align}

nodes.name: $L^\infty$ saving
nodes.statement: Next, our goal is to save over the trivial bound on $\sum_{d\leq D}\max_{(c, d)=1}\Big\lvert\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}(t/X)\Big\rvert$ when $t \in \mathfrak{m}$ and $D$ as large as possible. We use estimates from exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions from the works of Matom\"aki \cite{Mat}, Mikawa \cite{Mik}, and Ter\"{a}v\"{a}inen \cite{Ter} to handle those sums over primes in Part \ref{part: exp sum}.

nodes.name: Combine bounds
nodes.statement: Combining these $L^1$ and $L^\infty$ bounds, we will show that \begin{align} \notag \bigg(\sup_{t \in \mathfrak{m}}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c, d)=1}\bigg|\widehat{\Lambda}_{d,c}\bigg(\frac{-t}{X}\bigg)\bigg|\bigg)\sum_{t\in \mathfrak{m}}\dfrac{1}{X}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{t}{X}\bigg)\bigg| \ll_{A,b, \delta}\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{A}}. \end{align} This completes the rough outline of the proof of Theorem \ref{Main Theorem}.

nodes.name: Theorem 7 contains Theorems 1-3
nodes.statement: Note that we will establish a much more general theorem, Theorem \ref{Thm G}, for an arithmetic function $\mathfrak{f}$ satisfying some appropriate conditions in Part \ref{part: circle}. In particular, Theorem \ref{Thm G} will incorporate Theorems \ref{Main Theorem}, \ref{Main Theorem2}, and \ref{Main Theorem3} by choosing $\mathfrak{f}$ and other parameters appropriately.
nodes.section: 2 Set-up and outline of the proof

nodes.name: Sifting function
nodes.statement: Given a sequence of weights $\mathcal{C}=\big(c(n)\big)_{n=1}^\infty \subset \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ with $\sum_{n=1}^\infty c(n) <\infty$ and a set of primes $\mathcal{P}$, we consider the {\it sifting function}, \[S(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{P}, z) := \sum_{(n, P(z))=1}c(n),\] where for some real number $z>1$, \[P(z): = \prod_{\substack{p \leq z\\p \in \mathcal{P}}}p.\]
nodes.statement_short: $S(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{P},z)$ sums the weights $c(n)$ over $n$ free of primes $p\le z$ in $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Sifting parameter
nodes.statement: Here $z$ is often called the \emph{sifting parameter} in the sieve setting.

nodes.name: Congruence sums $C_d(x)$
nodes.statement: In order to proceed further, for any $x\geq 1$ and for each integer $d\geq 1$, we set \[C_d(x) := \sum_{\substack{n \leq x\\d|n}}c(n), \] and we impose the following {\it axioms of sieve theory}:

nodes.name: Sieve axiom (A1): density function
nodes.statement: For some multiplicative function $\mathfrak{g}$, we have \[C_d(x)= \dfrac{\mathfrak{g}(d)}{d}C(x) + {E}(d),\] where $C(x)$ can be interpreted as an approximation to $\sum_{n\leq x}c(n)$ and ${E}(d)$ is a real number which we think of as an error term.

nodes.name: Sieve axiom (A2): local density bound
nodes.statement: We assume that the multiplicative function $\mathfrak{g}$ satisfies $\mathfrak{g}(p) \leq \min\{2, p-1\}$ for all primes $p\in \mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Sieve axiom (A3): level of distribution
nodes.statement: There is a constant $A>0$, and a quantity $D\geq 1$ such that \[\sum_{d\leq D}\mu^2(d)|{E}(d)| \ll_{A}\dfrac{C(x)}{(\log x)^A}.\] If such an estimate holds, then we say $\mathcal{C}$ has {\it level of distribution} $D$.

nodes.name: Sieve axiom (A4): sieve dimension
nodes.statement: We have \[\sum_{\substack{p \leq x\\ p \in \mathcal{P}}}\dfrac{\mathfrak{g}(p)\log p}{p} = \varkappa\log x + O(1) \quad \text{for all $x$}.\] Here we say $\varkappa$ as the {\it dimension of the sieve}.

nodes.name: Upper bound sieve
nodes.statement: An arithmetic function $\lambda^+:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ that is supported on the set $\{d|P(z): \: d \leq D\}$ and satisfies the relation $(\lambda^+*1)(n) \geq 1_{(n,\: P(z))=1}$ is called an \emph{upper bound sieve of level $D$} for the set of primes $\mathcal{P}$.
differentia: supported on the set $\{d|P(z): \: d \leq D\}$

nodes.name: Lower bound sieve
nodes.statement: An arithmetic function $\lambda^-:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ that is supported on the set $\{d|P(z): \: d \leq D\}$ and satisfies the relation $1_{(n,\:P(z))=1} \geq (\lambda^-*1)(n)$ is called a \emph{lower bound sieve of level $D$} for the set of primes $\mathcal{P}$.
differentia: supported on the set $\{d|P(z): \: d \leq D\}$

nodes.name: Sieve weights
nodes.statement: We will refer to $\lambda^{\pm}$ as the \emph{sieve weights} or \emph{sifting weights} in this paper.

nodes.name: Semi-linear sieve
nodes.statement: Now we are ready to state the Fundamental Lemma of Sieve Theory in the special case when the dimension $\varkappa$ equals $1/2$, often referred to as the {\it semi-linear sieve} or the {\it half-dimensional sieve}.

nodes.name: Fundamental Lemma for the Semi-linear Sieve
nodes.statement: Consider a sequence $\mathcal{C}=\big(c(n)\big)_{n=1}^\infty$ of non-negative real numbers and a set of primes $\mathcal{P}$ satisfying axioms \ref{A1}, \ref{A2}, and \ref{A4} with $\varkappa = 1/2$. If $u_1>0$ and $D=z_1^{u_1}$, then there exist two arithmetic functions $\lambda^\pm_{\textup{sem}}: \mathbb{N}\rightarrow [-1, 1]$ supported on the set $\{d|P(z_1): d\leq D\}$, and we have \begin{equation} S(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{P}, z_1) \geq C(x)\bigg\{f_{\textup{sem}}(u_1) + o(1)\bigg\}\prod_{p\leq z_1,\: p\in \mathcal{P}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{\mathfrak{g}(p)}{p}\bigg) - \sum_{\substack{p|d \Rightarrow p \in \mathcal{P}\\ d\leq D}}\lambda^-_{\textup{sem}}(d){E}(d), \end{equation} and \begin{equation} S(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{P}, z_1) \leq C(x)\bigg\{F_{\textup{sem}}(u_1) + o(1)\bigg\}\prod_{p\leq z_1,\: p\in \mathcal{P}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{\mathfrak{g}(p)}{p}\bigg)+\sum_{\substack{p|d \Rightarrow p \in \mathcal{P}\\ d\leq D}}\lambda^+_{\textup{sem}}(d){E}(d), \end{equation} where $f_{\textup{sem}}, F_{\textup{sem}}$ are continuous functions in $u_1 = \log D/\log z_1$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{cases} \sqrt{u_1}F_{\textup{sem}}(u_1)=2\sqrt{e^\gamma/\pi} & \text{if}\quad 0 <u_1 \leq 2, \\ f_{\textup{sem}}(u_1) = 0 & \text{if}\quad 0<u_1\leq 1, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant, and for $1\leq u_1\leq 3$ we have \begin{equation} \dfrac{\sqrt{u_1}f_{\textup{sem}}(u_1)}{\sqrt{e^\gamma/\pi}}=\int_1^{u_1} \dfrac{\textup{d}y}{\sqrt{y(y-1)}}=\log \bigg(1+2(u_1-1)+2\sqrt{u_1(u_1-1)}\bigg). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Half-dimensional sieve: upper and lower bounds for $S(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{P},z_1)$ with explicit $F_{sem}, f_{sem}$ and remainder sums.
nodes.origin_citation: Friedlander-Iwaniec, Opera de Cribro, Thms 11.12-11.13 and Ch. 14
assumptions: a sequence $\mathcal{C}=\big(c(n)\big)_{n=1}^\infty$ of non-negative real numbers and a set of primes $\mathcal{P}$ satisfying axioms \ref{A1}, \ref{A2}, and \ref{A4} with $\varkappa = 1/2$
conclusions: there exist two arithmetic functions $\lambda^\pm_{\textup{sem}}: \mathbb{N}\rightarrow [-1, 1]$ supported on the set $\{d|P(z_1): d\leq D\}$
nodes.label: fundsemi

nodes.name: Proof of the Fundamental Lemma for the Semi-linear Sieve
nodes.statement: The proof follows from \cite[Theorem 11.12--Theorem 11.13 ]{opera}) with $\beta=1$ and \cite[Chapter 14 (pp. 275--276)]{opera}.

nodes.name: Partial well-factorability of semi-linear sieve
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon>0$ be small. Let $\delta\in (0, 10^{-3}]$ and let $\rho_{\textup{sem}}=\frac{3}{7}(1-4\delta)-\varepsilon$. Then the lower bound semi-linear sieve weights $\lambda_{\textup{sem}}^-$ as given in Lemma \ref{fundsemi} with level $X^{\rho_{\textup{sem}}}$ and sifting parameter $z_1\leq X^{1/3-2\delta-2\varepsilon^2}$ is supported in the set \begin{align} \mathfrak{D}^{-,\: \textup{sem}}=\{p_1\cdots p_r\leq X^{\rho_{\textup{sem}}}: z_1\geq p_1> \dotsc >p_r, p_1\cdots p_{2m-1}p_{2m}^2\leq X^{\rho_{\textup{sem}}}\: \forall \: m \geq 1\}, \end{align} where $p_1, \dotsc, p_r$ denote primes. In addition, for any $D_0\in [X^{1/3-2\delta-2\varepsilon^2}, X^{\rho_{\textup{sem}}}]$, every $d\in \mathfrak{D}^{-, \textup{sem}}\cap[X^{1/10}, X^{\rho_{\textup{sem}}}]$ can be factorized as $d=d_1d_2$ such that $d_1\in [X^{1/10}, D_0]$ and $d_1d_2^2\leq X^{1-4\delta-2\varepsilon^2}/D_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower semi-linear sieve weights of level $X^{3(1-4\delta)/7-\varepsilon}$ are supported on factorable $d=d_1d_2$ with controlled sizes.
conclusions: every $d\in \mathfrak{D}^{-, \textup{sem}}\cap[X^{1/10}, X^{\rho_{\textup{sem}}}]$ can be factorized as $d=d_1d_2$ such that $d_1\in [X^{1/10}, D_0]$ and $d_1d_2^2\leq X^{1-4\delta-2\varepsilon^2}/D_0$

nodes.name: Linear sieve
nodes.statement: Next, we state the Fundamental Lemma for the {\it linear sieve}, that is, for dimension $\varkappa=1$.

nodes.name: Fundamental Lemma for the Linear Sieve
nodes.statement: Consider a sequence $\mathcal{C} = \big(c(n)\big)_{n=1}^\infty\subset\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ and a set of primes $\mathcal{P}$ satisfying axioms \ref{A1}, \ref{A2}, and \ref{A4} with $\varkappa = 1$. If $u_2>0$ and $D=z_2^{u_2}$, then there exist two arithmetic functions $\lambda^\pm_{\textup{lin}}: \mathbb{N}\rightarrow [-1, 1]$ supported on the set $\{d|P(z_2): d\leq D\}$, and we have \begin{equation} S(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{P}, z_2) \geq C(x)\Big\{f_{\textup{lin}}(u_2) + o(1)\Big\}\prod_{p\leq z_2,\: p\in \mathcal{P}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{\mathfrak{g}(p)}{p}\bigg) - \sum_{\substack{p|d \Rightarrow p \in \mathcal{P}\\ d\leq D}}\lambda^-_{\textup{lin}}(d){E}(d), \end{equation} and \begin{equation} S(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{P}, z_2) \leq C(x)\Big\{F_{\textup{lin}}(u_2) + o(1)\Big\}\prod_{p\leq z_2,\: p\in \mathcal{P}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{\mathfrak{g}(p)}{p}\bigg) +\sum_{\substack{p|d \Rightarrow p \in \mathcal{P}\\ d\leq D}}\lambda^+_{\textup{lin}}(d){E}(d), \end{equation} where $f_{\textup{lin}}, F_{\textup{lin}}$ are continuous functions in $u_2 = \log D/\log z_2$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{cases} u_2 F_{\textup{lin}}(u_2)=2e^\gamma & \text{if}\quad 1 \leq u_2 \leq 3, \\ f_{\textup{lin}}(u_2) = 0 & \text{if}\quad 0<u_2\leq 2, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant.
nodes.statement_short: Linear sieve: upper and lower bounds for $S(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{P},z_2)$ with $F_{lin}, f_{lin}$ and remainder sums.

nodes.name: Proof of the Fundamental Lemma for the Linear Sieve
nodes.statement: The proof follows from \cite[Theorem 11.12--Theorem 11.13 ]{opera}) with $\beta=2$ and \cite[Chapter 12 (pp. 235--236)]{opera}.

nodes.name: Well-factorability of linear sieve
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon>0$ be small. Let $\delta\in (0, 10^{-3}]$ and let $\rho_{\textup{lin}}=\frac{1}{2}-2\delta-\varepsilon$. Then the upper bound linear sieve weights $\lambda_{\textup{lin}}^+$ as given in Lemma \ref{fundlin} with level $X^{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}$ and sifting parameter $z_2\leq X^{1/2}$ is supported in the set \begin{align} \mathfrak{D}^{+,\: \textup{lin}}=\{p_1\cdots p_r\leq X^{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}: z_2\geq p_1> \dotsc >p_r, p_1\cdots p_{2m-2}p_{2m-1}^3\leq X^{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}\: \forall \: m\geq 1\}, \end{align} where $p_1, \dotsc, p_r$ denote primes. In addition, for any $D_0 \in [X^{1/5}, X^{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}]$, every $d \in \mathfrak{D}^{+, \textup{lin}}\cap[X^{1/10}, X^{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}]$ can be factorized as $d=d_1d_2$ such that $d_1\in [X^{1/10}, D_0]$ and $d_1d_2^2\leq X^{1-4\delta-2\varepsilon^2}/D_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Upper linear sieve weights of level $X^{1/2-2\delta-\varepsilon}$ are supported on factorable $d=d_1d_2$ with controlled sizes.
conclusions: every $d \in \mathfrak{D}^{+, \textup{lin}}\cap[X^{1/10}, X^{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}]$ can be factorized as $d=d_1d_2$ such that $d_1\in [X^{1/10}, D_0]$ and $d_1d_2^2\leq X^{1-4\delta-2\varepsilon^2}/D_0$

nodes.name: Upper bound for primes $1+m^2+n^2$ with a missing digit
nodes.statement: Let $b$ be a sufficiently large odd integer and $r \in \mathcal{A}\cap[0, b)$ be such that $(r, b)=(r-1, b)=1$. Then, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{p<X\\p\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(p)1_{\mathbb{B}}(p-1)\ll_{b} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{3/2}}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound $\ll_b X^\zeta/(\log X)^{3/2}$ for missing-digit primes $p$ with $p-1\in\mathbb{B}$.
assumptions: $b$ be a sufficiently large odd integer
$r \in \mathcal{A}\cap[0, b)$ be such that $(r, b)=(r-1, b)=1$
nodes.label: PropUpper

nodes.name: Proof of the upper bound (Proposition 4.1)
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound semi-linear sieve on $\Lambda 1_{\mathcal{A}_r}$ over $p\equiv1$-shifted progressions, with level of distribution from Theorem 1, then Mertens.

nodes.name: Sifting set-up
nodes.statement: Let $z\in [2, X]$ be a parameter to be chosen later. We let \begin{align} \notag \mathcal{P}_3=\{p\equiv 3\imod 4, p \nmid b\} \quad \text{and} \quad P_3(z) = \prod_{\substack{p\leq z\\p\in \mathcal{P}_3}}p. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $z$ and the primes $\mathcal{P}_3\equiv 3 \bmod 4$.

nodes.name: Reduce to a sifted prime sum
nodes.statement: Then, we have \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{p<X\\p\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(p) 1_{\mathbb{B}}(p-1) &\leq \sum_{\substack{p<X\\(p-1, P_3(z))=1}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(p)\\ \notag &< \dfrac{10}{9\log X}\sum_{\substack{X^{9/10}<p<X\\(p-1, P_3(z))=1}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(p)\log p + X^{9/10}\\ &< \dfrac{10}{9\log X}\sum_{\substack{n<X\\(n-1, P_3(z))=1}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n) + X^{9/10}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the count by a sifted sum of $\Lambda 1_{\mathcal{A}_r}$.

nodes.name: Equation (4.1)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{p<X\\p\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(p) 1_{\mathbb{B}}(p-1) &\leq \sum_{\substack{p<X\\(p-1, P_3(z))=1}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(p)\\ \notag &< \dfrac{10}{9\log X}\sum_{\substack{X^{9/10}<p<X\\(p-1, P_3(z))=1}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(p)\log p + X^{9/10}\\ &< \dfrac{10}{9\log X}\sum_{\substack{n<X\\(n-1, P_3(z))=1}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n) + X^{9/10}.
nodes.label: upper1

nodes.name: Level of distribution from Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Next, for $d|P_3(z)$, we set \begin{align} \notag {E}(d)=\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv 1\imod d\\}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)- \dfrac{1}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n). \end{align} Therefore, by Theorem \ref{Main Theorem} with $D=X^{3/10}$, for any large real number $A>0$, we find that \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{d\leq X^{3/10}\\d|P_3(z)}}\lvert {E}(d)\rvert \ll \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Define $E(d)$ and bound its sum by Theorem 1 with $D=X^{3/10}$.

nodes.name: Apply the upper semi-linear sieve
nodes.statement: Now, we choose $c(n)=\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)$ for $n<X$ and $z_1=D=z=X^{3/10}$ in Lemma \ref{fundsemi}. Clearly, the sequence $c(n)$ satisfies the axioms of sieve theory with $\mathfrak{g}(d)=d/\varphi(d)$ and $\varkappa =1/2$. Therefore, by the upper bound semi-linear sieve \eqref{upper} with $u_1=1$, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{n<X\\(n-1, P_3(z))=1}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\leq&~\bigg(\dfrac{2e^{\gamma/2}}{\pi^{1/2}} + o(1)\bigg) \dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\prod_{\substack{p<z\\p\in \mathcal{P}_3}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p-1}\bigg)+ O\bigg(\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A}\bigg), \end{align} where $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the upper bound semi-linear sieve with $u_1=1$.

nodes.name: Combine estimates
nodes.statement: The above estimate together with the estimates from \eqref{upper1} and \eqref{upper2} allows us to obtain \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{p<X\\p\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(p)1_{\mathbb{B}}(p-1) \leq &~\bigg(\dfrac{2e^{\gamma/2}}{\pi^{1/2}} + o(1)\bigg) \dfrac{10b}{9\varphi(b)\log X}\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\prod_{\substack{p<z\\p\in \mathcal{P}_3}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p-1}\bigg)\\ \notag &+ O\bigg(\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A} + X^{9/10}\bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the reduction.

nodes.name: Mertens' estimate
nodes.statement: We can now use Mertens' estimate \cite[Theorem 3.4(c)]{kou} to the product over the primes (for example, see \cite[p.278]{opera} for a detailed estimate) and the fact that $\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)=X^\zeta/(b-1)$ to deduce that \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{p<X\\p\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(p) 1_{\mathbb{B}}(p-1) \ll_{b} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{3/2}} \end{align} as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Mertens' estimate gives the $(\log X)^{-3/2}$ bound.

nodes.name: Sieve set-up $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{P}_3$, $P_3(z)$ for the lower bound
nodes.statement: For $r\in \mathcal{A}\cap[0,b)$ with $\big(r(r-1), b\big)=1$, we set \begin{align} \begin{split} &\mathcal{F} ={\{p-1:\: p < X, \: p\in \mathcal{A}_r,\: p\equiv 3\imod 8\}},\\ \mathcal{P}_3 & =\{p\equiv 3\imod 4, p\nmid b\},\quad \text{and} \quad P_3(z)=\prod_{\substack{p<z\\p\in \mathcal{P}_3}}p. \end{split} \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Equation (4.3)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\mathcal{F} ={\{p-1:\: p < X, \: p\in \mathcal{A}_r,\: p\equiv 3\imod 8\}},\\ \mathcal{P}_3 & =\{p\equiv 3\imod 4, p\nmid b\},\quad \text{and} \quad P_3(z)=\prod_{\substack{p<z\\p\in \mathcal{P}_3}}p. \end{split}
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: setup F

nodes.name: Equation (4.4)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{p<X\\p\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(p)1_{\mathbb{B}}(p-1)\geq S(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{P}_3, X^{1/2})=\sum_{\substack{p<X\\(p-1,\: P_3(X^{1/2}))=1\\p\equiv 3\imod 8}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(p).
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: sieve lower

nodes.name: Sifting level $z=X^{1/\alpha}$
nodes.statement: For notational convenience, we set $z=X^{1/\alpha}$ for some $\alpha\in [2, 4)$.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Buchstab decomposition $S-T$
nodes.statement: By the Buchstab identity (see \cite[eqn (6.4)]{opera}), we have \begin{align} S(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{P}_3, \sqrt{X}) = S(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{P}_3, z)-\sum_{\substack{z<p_1\leq \sqrt{X}\\p_1\equiv 3\imod 4}}S(\mathcal{F}_{p_1}, \mathcal{P}_3, p_1)=:S-T. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Buchstab's identity writes the sifting function at $\sqrt X$ as $S-T$.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Equation (4.5)
nodes.statement: S(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{P}_3, \sqrt{X}) = S(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{P}_3, z)-\sum_{\substack{z<p_1\leq \sqrt{X}\\p_1\equiv 3\imod 4}}S(\mathcal{F}_{p_1}, \mathcal{P}_3, p_1)=:S-T.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: Buch

nodes.name: Expression for $T$
nodes.statement: Since $p-1$ has an even number of prime factors in the class $3\imod 4$ and by our choice of $z$, we can write the sum $T$ as \begin{align} \notag T=\sum_{p<X}\sum_{\substack{p-1=2n_1p_1p_2\\p_1,\: p_2\in \mathcal{P}_3\\p_2\geq p_1\geq X^{1/\alpha}\\n_1\in \mathcal{B}}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(p), \end{align} where $\mathcal{B}=\{n: p|n \Rightarrow p\equiv 1\imod 4\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $T$ counts $p$ with $p-1=2n_1p_1p_2$, $p_1,p_2\equiv 3 \bmod 4$, $p_2\ge p_1\ge X^{1/\alpha}$.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Sets $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{M}(\ell)$
nodes.statement: Following Matom\"aki \cite{Mat}, we define \begin{align} \mathcal{L}&=\{\ell =n_1p_1: n_1\leq X^{1-2/\alpha}, n_1\in \mathcal{B}, X^{1/\alpha}\leq p_1 <(X/n_1)^{1/2}, p_1\in \mathcal{P}_3\},\\ \intertext{and for each $\ell \in \mathcal{L}$,} \mathcal{M}(\ell)& ={\{m=2\ell p_2+1:\: m \in \mathcal{A}_r,\: p_2< X/2\ell, \: p_2\in \mathcal{P}_3,\: p_2\geq X^{1/\alpha}\}}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Equation (4.6)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{L}&=\{\ell =n_1p_1: n_1\leq X^{1-2/\alpha}, n_1\in \mathcal{B}, X^{1/\alpha}\leq p_1 <(X/n_1)^{1/2}, p_1\in \mathcal{P}_3\},
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: mathcalL

nodes.name: Equation (4.7)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{M}(\ell)& ={\{m=2\ell p_2+1:\: m \in \mathcal{A}_r,\: p_2< X/2\ell, \: p_2\in \mathcal{P}_3,\: p_2\geq X^{1/\alpha}\}}.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: mathcalMl

nodes.name: Bound for $T$ by sifting functions of $\mathcal{M}(\ell)$
nodes.statement:
This allows us to bound the sum $T$ as  egin{align} T\leq \sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\(\ell, b)=1}} igg(S(\mathcal{M}(\ell), \mathcal{P}(\ell), X^{1/
u}) + O(X^{1/
u}) igg), \end{align} where $\mathcal{P}(\ell)=\{p: p
mid 2b\ell\}$ and we will choose $
u$ appropriately later.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Equation (4.8)
nodes.statement: T\leq \sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\\(\ell, b)=1}}\bigg(S(\mathcal{M}(\ell), \mathcal{P}(\ell), X^{1/\nu}) + O(X^{1/\nu})\bigg),
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: Tsimple

nodes.name: The base $b$ must be odd
nodes.statement: Note that if $m\in \mathcal{M}(\ell)$ in \eqref{mathcalMl}, we have $2\ell p_2+1\equiv r\imod b$. Since $(r-1, b)=1$ this implies that $(2\ell p_2, b)=1$, which in turn restricts the base $b$ to be odd.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Lower bound for $S$ via the semi-linear sieve
nodes.statement: Assume the above sieve set-up. Let $\varepsilon>0$ be small. Let $\delta\in (0, 10^{-3}]$ and let $b$ be an odd integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$. Let $\alpha=(1/3-2\delta)^{-1}+\varepsilon$ be such that $\alpha\in [2, 4)$ and let $\rho_{\textup{sem}}\leq \frac{3}{7}(1-4\delta)-\varepsilon$. Then we have \begin{align} S\geq \dfrac{\mathfrak{S}+ o(1)}{(\log X)^{3/2}}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 3\imod 4}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p-1}\bigg)^{-1}I_{\textup{sem}}(\rho_{\textup{sem}}, \alpha)\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n), \end{align} where \begin{align} \mathfrak{S} &=\dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}\prod_{p\equiv 3\imod 4}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p^2}\bigg)^{1/2}\prod_{p\equiv 3\imod 4}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{(p-1)^2}\bigg) \end{align} and \begin{align} I_{\textup{sem}}(\rho_{\textup{sem}}, \alpha)&=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\rho_{\textup{sem}}}}\int_{1}^{\alpha \rho_{\textup{sem}}} \dfrac{\textup{d}y}{\sqrt{y(y-1)}}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound for $S$ of size $\mathfrak{S}I_{sem}(\rho_{sem},\alpha)(\log X)^{-3/2}$ times the count of $\mathcal{A}_r$.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
assumptions: $b$ be an odd integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$
nodes.label: PropAppS

nodes.name: Equation (4.9)
nodes.statement: S\geq \dfrac{\mathfrak{S}+ o(1)}{(\log X)^{3/2}}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 3\imod 4}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p-1}\bigg)^{-1}I_{\textup{sem}}(\rho_{\textup{sem}}, \alpha)\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n),
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: EqS1

nodes.name: Equation (4.10)
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{S} &=\dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}\prod_{p\equiv 3\imod 4}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p^2}\bigg)^{1/2}\prod_{p\equiv 3\imod 4}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{(p-1)^2}\bigg)
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: ac

nodes.name: Equation (4.11)
nodes.statement: I_{\textup{sem}}(\rho_{\textup{sem}}, \alpha)&=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\rho_{\textup{sem}}}}\int_{1}^{\alpha \rho_{\textup{sem}}} \dfrac{\textup{d}y}{\sqrt{y(y-1)}}.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: eq: isem

nodes.name: Upper bound for $T$ via the linear sieve
nodes.statement: Assume the above sieve set-up. Let $\varepsilon>0$ be small. Let $\delta\in (0, 10^{-3}]$ and let $b$ be an odd integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$. Let $\alpha=(1/3-2\delta)^{-1} + \varepsilon$ be such that $\alpha\in [2, 4)$ and let $\rho_{\textup{lin}}\leq \frac{1}{2}-2\delta-\varepsilon$. Then we have \begin{align} T\leq \dfrac{10\mathfrak{S}+o(1)}{9(\log X)^{3/2}} \dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 3\imod 4}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p-1}\bigg)^{-1}I_{\textup{lin}}(\rho_{\textup{lin}}, \alpha)\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n), \end{align} where $\mathfrak{S}$ is given by the relation \eqref{ac} and \begin{align} I_{\textup{lin}}(\rho_{\textup{lin}}, \alpha)=\dfrac{1}{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}\int_{2}^\alpha\dfrac{\log (y-1)}{y(1-y/\alpha)^{1/2}}\textup{d}y. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound for $T$ of size $\frac{10}{9}\mathfrak{S}I_{lin}(\rho_{lin},\alpha)(\log X)^{-3/2}$ times the count of $\mathcal{A}_r$.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
assumptions: $b$ be an odd integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$
nodes.label: PropAppT

nodes.name: Equation (4.12)
nodes.statement: T\leq \dfrac{10\mathfrak{S}+o(1)}{9(\log X)^{3/2}} \dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 3\imod 4}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p-1}\bigg)^{-1}I_{\textup{lin}}(\rho_{\textup{lin}}, \alpha)\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n),
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: EqT1

nodes.name: Equation (4.13)
nodes.statement: I_{\textup{lin}}(\rho_{\textup{lin}}, \alpha)=\dfrac{1}{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}\int_{2}^\alpha\dfrac{\log (y-1)}{y(1-y/\alpha)^{1/2}}\textup{d}y.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.
nodes.label: eq: ilin

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4 assuming Propositions 4.2 and 4.3
nodes.statement_short: Combine Buchstab $S-T$ with the bounds of Propositions 4.2 and 4.3; a numerical check shows $I_{sem}-\frac{10}{9}I_{lin}>0$.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Combine $S$ and $T$ bounds
nodes.statement_short: Insert the bounds for $S$ and $T$ into the Buchstab decomposition.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Numerical positivity
nodes.statement: A simple numerical computation yields that \begin{align} \notag I_{\textup{sem}}(\rho_{\textup{sem}}, \alpha)-\dfrac{10}{9}\cdot I_{\textup{lin}}(\rho_{\textup{lin}}, \alpha)>1.60492-1.4566=0.1482 > 0 \end{align} for $\rho_{\textup{sem}}=3(1-4\delta)/7-\varepsilon$, $\rho_{\textup{lin}}=1/2-2\delta-\varepsilon$, $\alpha=(1/3-2\delta)^{-1} +\varepsilon$, $\delta=1/1000$ with $\varepsilon>0$ small.
nodes.statement_short: Numerically $I_{sem}-\frac{10}{9}I_{lin}>0.1482$.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement: Hence, we obtain \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{p<X\\p\equiv r\imod b}}1_{\mathcal{A}}(p)1_{\mathbb{B}}(p-1)\gg \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{3/2}}. \end{align} This establishes the lower bound in Theorem \ref{Main TheoremApp}. Along with Proposition \ref{PropUpper}, this completes the proof of Theorem \ref{Main TheoremApp}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the lower bound; with Proposition 4.1 this proves Theorem 4.
nodes.section: 4.2.1 Sieve set-up for the lower bound.

nodes.name: Mertens-type product over primes $3 \bmod 4$
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align} \notag \prod_{\substack{p\leq y\\p\equiv 3\imod 4}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{\varphi(p)}\bigg)=2C_2C_3\Big(1+o(1)\Big)\bigg(\dfrac{\pi e^{-\gamma}}{\log y}\bigg)^{1/2} \quad \text{as} \quad y\rightarrow\infty, \end{align} where $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant, \begin{align} \notag C_2=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\prod_{p\equiv 3\imod 4}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p^2}\bigg)^{1/2}\quad \text{and}\quad C_3=\prod_{p\equiv 3\imod 4}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{(p-1)^2}\bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Asymptotic for $\prod_{p\le y, p\equiv 3 (4)}(1-1/\varphi(p))$ as $2C_2C_3(\pi e^{-\gamma}/\log y)^{1/2}$.
nodes.label: Aux1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement: The proof is standard and can be easily derived following \cite[pp.~277--278]{opera}.
nodes.statement_short: Standard; follows Opera de Cribro pp. 277-278.

nodes.name: Asymptotic for the weighted sum over $\mathcal{L}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be as in \eqref{mathcalL} and let $\alpha \in [2, 4)$. For any positive integer $n\geq 3$, let \begin{align} \mathfrak{t}(n) = \prod_{\substack{p|n\\ p>2}}\dfrac{p-1}{p-2}. \end{align} Then, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\\ (\ell, 2b)=1}}\dfrac{\mathfrak{t}(\ell)}{\ell \log (X/\ell)}=\dfrac{1+o(1)}{(\log X)^{1/2}}\dfrac{C_2}{2C_1}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 1\imod 4}}\bigg(1+\dfrac{1}{p-2}\bigg)^{-1}\int_{2}^\alpha \dfrac{\log (y-1)}{y(1-y/\alpha)^{1/2}}\textup{d}y, \end{align} where \begin{align} \notag C_2=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\prod_{p\equiv 3\imod 4}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p^2}\bigg)^{1/2}\quad \text{and}\quad C_1=\prod_{p\equiv 1\imod 4}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{(p-1)^2}\bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Asymptotic for $\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}}\mathfrak{t}(\ell)/(\ell\log(X/\ell))$ in terms of $\int_2^\alpha \log(y-1)/(y(1-y/\alpha)^{1/2})dy$.
nodes.label: Aux2

nodes.name: Equation (4.14)
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{t}(n) = \prod_{\substack{p|n\\ p>2}}\dfrac{p-1}{p-2}.
nodes.label: eq: mathfrakt

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement: The proof follows from the proof of \cite[Lemma 5]{Mat2} in conjunction with \cite[Satz 1]{Wir} to incorporate the extra condition $(\ell, 2b)=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Adapt Matomäki's Lemma 5 with Wirsing's Satz 1 for the condition $(\ell,2b)=1$.

nodes.name: Semi-linear sieve equidistribution estimate
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon>0$ be small. Let $\delta \in (0, 10^{-3}]$ and let $b$ be an odd integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$. Let $r\in \mathcal{A}\cap[0, b)$ with $(r(r-1), b)=1$. Let $\lambda^-_{\textup{sem}}$ be as in Lemma \ref{fundsemi} and Lemma \ref{wellfacsem} with $z_1\leq X^{1/3-2\delta-2\varepsilon^2}$ and $D=X^{\rho_{\textup{sem}}}$, where $\rho_{\textup{sem}}=3(1-4\delta)/7-\varepsilon$. Then for any $A>0$, we have \begin{align}\notag \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,2b)=1}}\lambda^-_{\textup{sem}}(d)\Bigg(\sum_{\substack{n < X\\n\equiv 1 \imod d\\n\equiv 3\imod 8}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n) - \dfrac{1}{4\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\Bigg) \ll_{A, b, \delta, \varepsilon} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A}. \end{align}

We can then use Theorem \ref{Hyp1} and the fact that the contribution of prime powers is negligible to bound the error term $E_1(d)$. In fact, using Chebyshev's estimate \cite[Theorem 2.4]{kou}, the contribution of prime powers can be bounded by \[\ll \sum_{d\leq X^{\frac{3}{7}(1-4\delta)-\varepsilon}}\sum_{\substack{p^m<X\\ p\equiv 1\imod d\\ p\equiv 3\imod 8\\ m\geq 2}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(p)\log p \ll (\log X)\sum_{d\leq X^{\frac{3}{7}(1-4\delta)-\varepsilon}}\sum_{p\leq X^{1/2}}1 \ll X^{13/14-12\delta/7},\] which is admissible. nodes.name: Small $p_2$ via Chebyshev
nodes.statement: Next, we use Chebyshev's bound \cite[Theorem 2.4]{kou} for the sum over primes $p_2$. Note that, since $\alpha=(1/3-2\delta)^{-1} + \varepsilon$, by \eqref{mathcalL}, we have \begin{align} \mathcal{L} \subset [X^{1/\alpha}, X^{1-1/\alpha}] \subset[X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}, X^{2/3+2\delta +\varepsilon}]. \end{align} This allows us to bound the second sum as \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\\(\ell, b)=1}}\sideset{}{^\flat}\sum_{\substack{p_2\leq (X/\ell)^{9/10}}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(2\ell p_2 +1)\ll \sum_{\ell\in [X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}, X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}]}\dfrac{(X/\ell)^{9/10}}{\log (X/\ell)} \ll X^{29/30+\delta/5+\varepsilon}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Small $p_2$ contribute $O(X^{29/30+\delta/5+\varepsilon})$.

nodes.name: Equation (4.25)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{L} \subset [X^{1/\alpha}, X^{1-1/\alpha}] \subset[X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}, X^{2/3+2\delta +\varepsilon}].
nodes.label: Range: L

nodes.name: Reduced bound for $T$
nodes.statement: The above estimates yield \begin{align} T\leq \dfrac{10}{9}\sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\\(\ell, b)=1}}\dfrac{1}{\log (X/\ell)}\sideset{}{^{\flat\flat}}\sum_{\substack{n< X/2\ell}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(2\ell n +1) + O\bigg(X^{29/30+\delta/5+\varepsilon} + \#\mathcal{L}X^{1/\nu}\bigg), \end{align} where $\sum^{\flat\flat}$ denotes a sum over values of $n$ satisfying \[\ell n\equiv 1\imod 4 \quad \text{and} \quad \big(2\ell n + 1, P_{\ell}(X^{1/\nu})\big)=1.\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduced bound for $T$.

nodes.name: Equation (4.26)
nodes.statement: T\leq \dfrac{10}{9}\sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\\(\ell, b)=1}}\dfrac{1}{\log (X/\ell)}\sideset{}{^{\flat\flat}}\sum_{\substack{n< X/2\ell}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(2\ell n +1) + O\bigg(X^{29/30+\delta/5+\varepsilon} + \#\mathcal{L}X^{1/\nu}\bigg),
nodes.label: T0

nodes.name: Apply the upper linear sieve
nodes.statement_short: Define $E_2(d)$ and apply the upper bound linear sieve.

nodes.name: Equation (4.27)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \sideset{}{^{\flat\flat}}\sum_{\substack{n< X/2\ell}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(2\ell n +1)\leq \dfrac{b}{4\varphi(b)}\big(F_{\textup{lin}}(u_2)+o(1)\big) &V_{\textup{lin}}(X^{1/\nu}) \dfrac{1}{\ell}\sum_{n<X}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\\ &+ \sum_{\substack{d\leq X^{u_2/\nu}\\(d,2\ell b)=1}}\lambda^+_{\textup{lin}}(d){E}_2(d), \end{aligned}
nodes.label: Sl

nodes.name: Mertens for $V_{lin}$
nodes.statement:
Since $(\ell, b)=1$ in \eqref{T0}, we may use Mertens' theorem \cite[Theorem 3.4(c)]{kou} to obtain  egin{align} V_{	extup{lin}}(X^{1/
u}) = \prod_{\substack{p< X^{1/
u}\ (p, 2\ell b)=1}} igg(1-\dfrac{1}{\varphi(p)} igg)= ig(1+o(1) ig)\dfrac{2
u C_1C_3e^{-\gamma}\mathfrak{t}(\ell)\mathfrak{t}(b)}{\log X}, \end{align} where $\mathfrak{t}(n)$ is given by \eqref{eq: mathfrakt},  egin{align} C_1 &= \prod_{p\equiv 1 \imod 4} igg(1-\dfrac{1}{(p-1)^2} igg), \quad 	ext{and} \quad C_3 = \prod_{p\equiv 3\imod 4} igg(1-\dfrac{1}{(p-1)^2} igg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate $V_{lin}$ with Mertens' theorem.

nodes.name: Equation (4.28)
nodes.statement:
V_{	extup{lin}}(X^{1/
u}) = \prod_{\substack{p< X^{1/
u}\ (p, 2\ell b)=1}} igg(1-\dfrac{1}{\varphi(p)} igg)= ig(1+o(1) ig)\dfrac{2
u C_1C_3e^{-\gamma}\mathfrak{t}(\ell)\mathfrak{t}(b)}{\log X},
nodes.label: Eq: Vlin

nodes.name: Equation (4.29)
nodes.statement: C_1 &= \prod_{p\equiv 1 \imod 4}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{(p-1)^2}\bigg), \quad \text{and} \quad C_3 = \prod_{p\equiv 3\imod 4}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{(p-1)^2}\bigg).
nodes.label: C_1C_3

nodes.name: Organise the remainder
nodes.statement: Now we take $u_2=\rho_{\textup{lin}} \nu$ in the linear sieve, where $\rho_{\textup{lin}}$ corresponds to the level of the upper bound sieve in Theorem \ref{Hyp2}. Next, using \eqref{Range: L}, we write \begin{align} \notag \sum_{d\leq X^{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}}\lambda^+_{\textup{lin}}(d)\sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\\(\ell, 2bd)=1}}\dfrac{1}{\log (X/\ell)}{E}_2(d)&=\sum_{d\leq X^{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}}\lambda^+_{\textup{lin}}(d)\sum_{\substack{X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}<\ell\leq X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}\\(\ell, 2bd)=1}}\dfrac{1_{\mathcal{L}}(\ell)}{\log (X/\ell)}{E}_2(d). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the remainder sum over $\ell$.

nodes.name: Remainder via Theorem 6
nodes.statement: We do a dyadic decomposition on the range of $\ell$, say $\ell \sim L$ with $L\in [X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}, X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}]$. Since the number of such dyadic intervals are at most $\log X$, we use Theorem \ref{Hyp2} with $\mathfrak{h}(\ell) = 1_{\mathcal{L}}(\ell)/\log (X/\ell)$ for $\ell\sim L$ to bound the above expression as \begin{align} \notag \sum_{d\leq X^{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}}\lambda^+_{\textup{lin}}(d)\sum_{\substack{X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}<\ell\leq X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}\\(\ell, 2bd)=1}}\mathfrak{h}(\ell){E}_2(d)&\ll (\log X)\bigg|\sum_{d\leq X^{\rho_{\textup{lin}}}}\lambda^+_{\textup{lin}}(d)\sum_{\substack{\ell \sim L\\(\ell, 2bd)=1}}\mathfrak{h}(\ell){E}_2(d)\bigg|\\ \notag &\ll_{A, b, \delta, \varepsilon} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A}, \end{align} which is admissible.
nodes.statement_short: Dyadic split in $\ell$ and Theorem 6 bound the remainder.

nodes.name: Main term for $T$
nodes.statement:
From \eqref{T0}, \eqref{Sl} and using the above bound for the error term, we have that  egin{align} 
otag T \leq &~\dfrac{10}{9}\cdot \dfrac{b}{4\varphi(b)} ig(F_{	extup{lin}}(u_2)+o(1) ig)\cdot \sum_{n<X}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\(\ell, b)=1}}\dfrac{V_{	extup{lin}}(X^{1/
u})}{\ell \log(X/\ell)}\ 
otag & + O_{A, b, \delta, \varepsilon} igg(\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A} + X^{29/30+\delta/5+\varepsilon} + \#\mathcal{L}X^{1/
u} igg)\ 
otag\leq &~\dfrac{10}{9}\cdot \dfrac{
u\cdot C_1C_3e^{-\gamma}}{2\log X}\cdot \dfrac{b\cdot \mathfrak{t}(b)}{\varphi(b)} ig(F_{	extup{lin}}(u_2)+o(1) ig)\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\(\ell, 2b)=1}}\dfrac {\mathfrak{t}(\ell)}{\ell \log (X/\ell)}\ &+ O_{A, b, \delta, \varepsilon} igg(\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A} + X^{29/30+\delta/5+\varepsilon} + \#\mathcal{L}X^{1/
u} igg), \end{align} where we have used the asymptotic formula for $V_{	extup{lin}}(X^{1/
u})$ from the relation \eqref{Eq: Vlin} in the last line.
nodes.statement_short: Collect the main term.

nodes.name: Equation (4.30)
nodes.statement:
otag T \leq &~\dfrac{10}{9}\cdot \dfrac{b}{4\varphi(b)} ig(F_{	extup{lin}}(u_2)+o(1) ig)\cdot \sum_{n<X}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\(\ell, b)=1}}\dfrac{V_{	extup{lin}}(X^{1/
u})}{\ell \log(X/\ell)}\ 
otag & + O_{A, b, \delta, \varepsilon} igg(\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A} + X^{29/30+\delta/5+\varepsilon} + \#\mathcal{L}X^{1/
u} igg)\ 
otag\leq &~\dfrac{10}{9}\cdot \dfrac{
u\cdot C_1C_3e^{-\gamma}}{2\log X}\cdot \dfrac{b\cdot \mathfrak{t}(b)}{\varphi(b)} ig(F_{	extup{lin}}(u_2)+o(1) ig)\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\(\ell, 2b)=1}}\dfrac {\mathfrak{t}(\ell)}{\ell \log (X/\ell)}\ &+ O_{A, b, \delta, \varepsilon} igg(\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A} + X^{29/30+\delta/5+\varepsilon} + \#\mathcal{L}X^{1/
u} igg),
nodes.label: Tefin

nodes.name: Sum over $\ell$ via Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement: Next, by Lemma \ref{Aux2}, we have \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\\(\ell, 2b)=1}}\dfrac {\mathfrak{t}(\ell)}{\ell \log (X/\ell)}=\dfrac{(1+o(1))C_2}{2C_1(\log X)^{1/2}}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 1\imod 4}}\bigg(1+\dfrac{1}{p-2}\bigg)^{-1}\int_{2}^\alpha\dfrac{\log (y-1)}{y(1-y/\alpha)^{1/2}}\text{d}y, \end{align} where $C_2$ is as in the relation \eqref{A} and $C_1$ is given by \eqref{C_1C_3}.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the $\ell$-sum by Lemma 4.5.

nodes.name: Equation (4.31)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{\ell \in \mathcal{L}\\(\ell, 2b)=1}}\dfrac {\mathfrak{t}(\ell)}{\ell \log (X/\ell)}=\dfrac{(1+o(1))C_2}{2C_1(\log X)^{1/2}}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 1\imod 4}}\bigg(1+\dfrac{1}{p-2}\bigg)^{-1}\int_{2}^\alpha\dfrac{\log (y-1)}{y(1-y/\alpha)^{1/2}}\text{d}y,
nodes.label: tlem

nodes.name: Choose parameters
nodes.statement:
We choose $u_2=5/2$, so that $F_{	extup{lin}}(u_2)=4e^\gamma/5$. As by our choice, $ho_{	extup{lin}}=1/2-2\delta-\varepsilon$, we can choose $
u=5$. Note that since $
u=5, \#\mathcal{L} \leq X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon>0$ is small enough, $\delta\in (0, 10^{-3}]$, and $\zeta$ tends to $1$ as $b ightarrow \infty$, we have that  egin{align} \#\mathcal{L}X^{1/
u}, X^{29/30+\delta/5+\varepsilon} \ll_{A, \delta, \varepsilon} \dfrac{X^\zeta}{(\log X)^A}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Choose $u_2=5/2$, $\nu=5$; error terms are admissible.

nodes.name: Equation (4.32)
nodes.statement: \#\mathcal{L}X^{1/\nu}, X^{29/30+\delta/5+\varepsilon} \ll_{A, \delta, \varepsilon} \dfrac{X^\zeta}{(\log X)^A}.
nodes.label: tefin2

nodes.name: Conclude bound for $T$
nodes.statement: Therefore, we substitute \eqref{tlem} and \eqref{tefin2} in \eqref{Tefin} to obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} T\leq &~\dfrac{10\mathfrak{S}+o(1)}{9(\log X)^{3/2}} \dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p>2}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p-1}\bigg)^{-1}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 1\imod 4}}\bigg(1+\dfrac{1}{p-2}\bigg)^{-1}I_{\textup{lin}}(\rho_{\textup{lin}}, \alpha)\\ &\times \sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n), \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $I_{\textup{lin}}(\rho_{\textup{lin}}, \alpha)$ is given by \eqref{eq: ilin} and $\mathfrak{S}=C_2C_3/2$ is given by the relation \eqref{mathfrakS}. Hence, the estimate \eqref{tfin} along with the fact that \[\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p>2}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p-1}\bigg)^{-1}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 1\imod 4}}\bigg(1+\dfrac{1}{p-2}\bigg)^{-1}=\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 3\imod 4}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p-1}\bigg)^{-1}\] yields the required bound for the sum $T$.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute to obtain the bound for $T$.

nodes.name: Equation (4.33)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} T\leq &~\dfrac{10\mathfrak{S}+o(1)}{9(\log X)^{3/2}} \dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p>2}}\bigg(1-\dfrac{1}{p-1}\bigg)^{-1}\prod_{\substack{p|b\\p\equiv 1\imod 4}}\bigg(1+\dfrac{1}{p-2}\bigg)^{-1}I_{\textup{lin}}(\rho_{\textup{lin}}, \alpha)\\ &\times \sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n), \end{aligned}
nodes.label: tfin

nodes.name: Sum of $\min(N, 1/\|m\theta\|)$
nodes.statement: Let $\theta = a/q + \beta$ with $(a, q)=1$ and $0< |\beta| < 1/q^2$. Then for any $M, N \geq 2$, we have \begin{equation} \notag \sum_{m=1}^M\min \bigg(N, \dfrac{1}{\lVert m\theta \rVert}\bigg) \ll \bigg(M + MNq\lvert \beta\rvert + \dfrac{1}{q\lvert \beta \rvert}\bigg)(\log 2qM). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Standard bound for $\sum_{m\le M}\min(N,\|m\theta\|^{-1})$ keeping the dependence on $\beta$.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate
nodes.label: lemma1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: The proof of the lemma is a standard one. However, we need a variant of it to take advantage of $\beta$ in the sum. For a detailed proof, see \cite[Lemma 4.1]{May2}.
nodes.statement_short: Standard; see Maynard, Lemma 4.1.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate

nodes.name: Hybrid bound for $\sum_{m\le M}\min(X/m+1, 1/\|m\theta\|)$
nodes.statement: Let $\theta = a/q + \beta$ with $(a, q)=1$ and $|\beta| < 1/q^2$. Then for any $M\geq 1$, we have \begin{align} \sum_{m\leq M}\min\bigg(\dfrac{X}{m}+1,\dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X}+ \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)(\log 2qM)^2, \end{align} where $H=1+|\beta|X$.
nodes.statement_short: $\sum_{m\le M}\min(X/m+1,\|m\theta\|^{-1})\ll X(M/X+qH/X+1/(qH))(\log 2qM)^2$ with $H=1+|\beta|X$.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate
nodes.label: Corollary1

nodes.name: Equation (5.1)
nodes.statement: \sum_{m\leq M}\min\bigg(\dfrac{X}{m}+1,\dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X}+ \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)(\log 2qM)^2,
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate
nodes.label: cor1eq

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.2
nodes.statement: If $\beta\neq 0$, we perform a dyadic decomposition and then apply Lemma \ref{lemma1} to obtain \begin{align} \sum_{m\leq M}\min \bigg(\dfrac{X}{m}+1,\dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) &\ll X\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + q\lvert\beta\rvert + \dfrac{1}{Xq\lvert\beta\rvert}\bigg)(\log 2qM)^2. \end{align} Next, for all $\beta$, we apply \cite[Lemma 13.7]{iwakow} to obtain \begin{align} \sum_{m\leq M}\bigg(\dfrac{X}{m} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{1}{q} + \dfrac{q}{X}\bigg)(\log 2qM). \end{align} Combining the estimates from inequalities \eqref{cor5.2i} and\eqref{cor5.2ii}, we have \begin{align} \sum_{m\leq M}\bigg(\dfrac{X}{m} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) \ll X\bigg\{\dfrac{M}{X} + \min\bigg(q|\beta| + \dfrac{1}{Xq|\beta|}, \dfrac{1}{q} + \dfrac{q}{X}\bigg)\bigg\}(\log 2qM)^2. \end{align} Next, we note that \begin{align} \min\bigg(\dfrac{1}{q}, \dfrac{1}{Xq|\beta|}\bigg)\leq \dfrac{2}{q(1+|\beta|X)}. \end{align} Therefore, using \eqref{cor5.2iv} and recalling that $|\beta|<1/q^2$, we obtain \begin{align}\notag \min\bigg(q|\beta| + \dfrac{1}{Xq|\beta|}, \dfrac{1}{q} + \dfrac{q}{X}\bigg)\ll q|\beta| + \dfrac{q}{X} + \dfrac{1}{q(1+|\beta|X)} = \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}, \end{align} where $H=1+|\beta|X$. Substituting the above inequality in \eqref{cor5.2iii} completes the proof of the corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemma 5.1 (after a dyadic split, for $\beta\ne0$) with Iwaniec-Kowalski Lemma 13.7 and take the minimum.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate

nodes.name: Case $\beta\ne 0$ via Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: If $\beta\neq 0$, we perform a dyadic decomposition and then apply Lemma \ref{lemma1} to obtain \begin{align} \sum_{m\leq M}\min \bigg(\dfrac{X}{m}+1,\dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) &\ll X\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + q\lvert\beta\rvert + \dfrac{1}{Xq\lvert\beta\rvert}\bigg)(\log 2qM)^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: For $\beta\ne0$ apply Lemma 5.1 dyadically.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate

nodes.name: Equation (5.2)
nodes.statement: \sum_{m\leq M}\min \bigg(\dfrac{X}{m}+1,\dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) &\ll X\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + q\lvert\beta\rvert + \dfrac{1}{Xq\lvert\beta\rvert}\bigg)(\log 2qM)^2.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate
nodes.label: cor5.2i

nodes.name: Bound for all $\beta$
nodes.statement: Next, for all $\beta$, we apply \cite[Lemma 13.7]{iwakow} to obtain \begin{align} \sum_{m\leq M}\bigg(\dfrac{X}{m} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{1}{q} + \dfrac{q}{X}\bigg)(\log 2qM). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Iwaniec-Kowalski Lemma 13.7.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate

nodes.name: Equation (5.3)
nodes.statement: \sum_{m\leq M}\bigg(\dfrac{X}{m} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{1}{q} + \dfrac{q}{X}\bigg)(\log 2qM).
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate
nodes.label: cor5.2ii

nodes.name: Take the minimum
nodes.statement: Combining the estimates from inequalities \eqref{cor5.2i} and\eqref{cor5.2ii}, we have \begin{align} \sum_{m\leq M}\bigg(\dfrac{X}{m} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) \ll X\bigg\{\dfrac{M}{X} + \min\bigg(q|\beta| + \dfrac{1}{Xq|\beta|}, \dfrac{1}{q} + \dfrac{q}{X}\bigg)\bigg\}(\log 2qM)^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Combine the two bounds via a minimum.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate

nodes.name: Equation (5.4)
nodes.statement: \sum_{m\leq M}\bigg(\dfrac{X}{m} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\|m\theta\|}\bigg) \ll X\bigg\{\dfrac{M}{X} + \min\bigg(q|\beta| + \dfrac{1}{Xq|\beta|}, \dfrac{1}{q} + \dfrac{q}{X}\bigg)\bigg\}(\log 2qM)^2.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate
nodes.label: cor5.2iii

nodes.name: Simplify the minimum
nodes.statement: Next, we note that \begin{align} \min\bigg(\dfrac{1}{q}, \dfrac{1}{Xq|\beta|}\bigg)\leq \dfrac{2}{q(1+|\beta|X)}. \end{align} Therefore, using \eqref{cor5.2iv} and recalling that $|\beta|<1/q^2$, we obtain \begin{align}\notag \min\bigg(q|\beta| + \dfrac{1}{Xq|\beta|}, \dfrac{1}{q} + \dfrac{q}{X}\bigg)\ll q|\beta| + \dfrac{q}{X} + \dfrac{1}{q(1+|\beta|X)} = \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}, \end{align} where $H=1+|\beta|X$. Substituting the above inequality in \eqref{cor5.2iii} completes the proof of the corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Simplify the minimum to $qH/X+1/(qH)$.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate

nodes.name: Equation (5.5)
nodes.statement: \min\bigg(\dfrac{1}{q}, \dfrac{1}{Xq|\beta|}\bigg)\leq \dfrac{2}{q(1+|\beta|X)}.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate
nodes.label: cor5.2iv

nodes.name: Bilinear estimate
nodes.statement: Let $M, N \geq 1$ be such that $MN\leq X$. Let $\theta = a/q + \beta$ for some $(a, q)=1$ and $|\beta| < 1/q^2$. Suppose ${\alpha}_1$ and ${\alpha}_2$ are two arithmetic functions supported in $[1, M]$ and $[1, N]$, respectively. Then we have \begin{align}\notag \sum_{n\leq X}({\alpha} _1*{\alpha}_2)(n)e(n \theta) \ll X^{1/2}\lVert {\alpha}_1 \rVert_2 \lVert {\alpha}_2 \rVert_2\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{N}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH} \bigg)^{1/2}(\log 2qX), \end{align} where $H=1+|\beta|X$.
nodes.statement_short: Bilinear exponential sum bound $X^{1/2}\|\alpha_1\|_2\|\alpha_2\|_2(M/X+N/X+qH/X+1/(qH))^{1/2}\log(2qX)$.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate
assumptions: ${\alpha}_1$ and ${\alpha}_2$ are two arithmetic functions supported in $[1, M]$ and $[1, N]$, respectively
nodes.label: bilinear lemma

nodes.name: Proof of the bilinear estimate
nodes.statement: The proof follows by combining the argument of \cite[Theorem 23.6]{kou} with Lemma \ref{lemma1} and Corollary \ref{Corollary1}.
nodes.statement_short: Koukoulopoulos' Theorem 23.6 argument with Lemma 5.1 and Corollary 5.2.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate

nodes.name: Matomäki's lemma
nodes.statement: Let $M, N\geq 1$ be such that $M, N\leq X$. Let $\theta= a/q + \beta$ with $(a, q)=1$, $|\beta\rvert <1/q^2$ and $q<X$. Then for any $\psi>0$, one has \begin{align} \notag M\sum_{m\sim M}\sum_{n\sim N}\uptau_3(n)\min\bigg(\dfrac{X}{m^2n} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\lVert m^2n \theta \rVert}\bigg)\ll &~M^2N(\log X)^3\\ \notag & + X\bigg(\dfrac{1}{M} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/2-\psi}(\log X)^8, \end{align} where $H=1+|\beta|X$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound for $M\sum_{m\sim M}\sum_{n\sim N}\uptau_3(n)\min(X/(m^2n)+1,\|m^2n\theta\|^{-1})$.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate
assumptions: $M, N\geq 1$ be such that $M, N\leq X$
nodes.label: Mikawa

nodes.name: Proof of Matomäki's lemma
nodes.statement: The proof follows from the argument of \cite[Lemma 8]{Mat} in conjunction with Lemma \ref{lemma1} and Corollary \ref{Corollary1}.
nodes.statement_short: Matomäki's Lemma 8 argument with Lemma 5.1 and Corollary 5.2.
nodes.section: 5 Preliminary estimates and Type I estimate

nodes.name: Type I estimate
nodes.statement: Let $v>0$. Let $D, M\geq 1$ be such that $DM<X$. Let $\theta=a/q+\beta$ with $(a, q)=1$, $\lvert \beta \rvert <1/q^2$ and $q<X$. Suppose ${\alpha}$ is an arithmetic function supported in $[1, M]$ and satisfies $\lvert {\alpha}\rvert \leq \uptau_{h_1}\cdot \log^{h_2}$ for some fixed integers $h_1\geq 1, h_2\geq 0$. Furthermore, let $h_3\geq 1$ be a fixed integer. Then, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{d\leq D}}\uptau_{h_3}(d)\cdot\max_{(c,d)=1}&\bigg\lvert \sum_{\substack{mn <X\\1\leq m\leq M\\mn\equiv c\imod d}}{\alpha}(m)(\log n)^ve(mn\theta)\bigg\rvert\\ \notag &\ll X\bigg(\dfrac{DM}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{(h_1+h_3)^2/2 + h_2+v + 1}, \end{align} where $H=1+|\beta|X$.
nodes.statement_short: Type I sums in progressions averaged over $d\le D$: $\ll X(DM/X+qH/X+1/(qH))^{1/2}$ up to logs.
assumptions: ${\alpha}$ is an arithmetic function supported in $[1, M]$ and satisfies $\lvert {\alpha}\rvert \leq \uptau_{h_1}\cdot \log^{h_2}$ for some fixed integers $h_1\geq 1, h_2\geq 0$
nodes.label: lemmatype1

nodes.name: Proof of the Type I estimate
nodes.statement_short: Partial summation and geometric sums reduce to $\min(X/(dm)+1,\|dm\theta\|^{-1})$; Cauchy-Schwarz and Corollary 5.2 finish.

nodes.name: Partial summation
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{S}_{\textup{Type I}}$ be the sum that we wish to estimate. Applying partial summation and then using the fact that $\sum_{n\leq y}e(nt) \ll \min(y, \|t\|^{-1})$ for any real numbers $y>1$ and $t$, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{n< X/m\\n\equiv c\overline{m}\imod {d}}}(\log n)^ve(mn\theta) &\ll (\log X/m)^v \min\bigg(\dfrac{X}{dm} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\|dm\theta\|}\bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the inner sum over $n$ by $\min(X/(dm)+1,\|dm\theta\|^{-1})$.

nodes.name: Sum over $d$ and $m$
nodes.statement: This implies that \begin{align} \notag |\mathcal{S}_{\textup{Type I}}|&\ll(\log X)^{v} \sum_{d\leq D}\uptau_{h_3}(d)\sum_{\substack{m\leq M}}|{\alpha}(m)|\min\bigg(\dfrac{X}{dm} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\lVert dm\theta\rVert}\bigg), \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Sum the pointwise bound over $d$ and $m$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz and Corollary 5.2
nodes.statement: Next, we write $d^\prime =dm$, so that $d^\prime \leq DM$. Then, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and Corollary \ref{Corollary1} along with the fact that $|{\alpha}| \leq \uptau_{h_1}\cdot \log^{h_2}$, we have \begin{align} \notag |\mathcal{S}_{\textup{Type I}}| & \ll(\log X)^{v+h_2}\bigg(X\sum_{d^\prime \leq DM}\dfrac{\uptau_{h_1+h_3}(d^\prime)^2}{d^\prime}\bigg)^{1/2}\cdot \bigg(\sum_{d^\prime \leq DM}\min\bigg(\dfrac{X}{d^\prime} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\lVert d^\prime \theta\rVert}\bigg)\bigg)^{1/2}\\ \notag & \ll (\log X)^{v+h_2} X(\log X)^{(h_1+h_3)^2/2}\bigg(\dfrac{DM}{X}+ \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X), \end{align} where we have used the fact that $\sum_{n\leq y}\uptau_h(n)^2/n \ll (\log y)^{h^2}$ for any real number $y\geq 2$ and for any integer $h\geq 1$. The above estimate on simplification yields the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Merge $d'=dm$, apply Cauchy-Schwarz and Corollary 5.2.

nodes.name: Point wise Type II estimate
nodes.statement: Let $M, N\geq 1$ be such that $MN\leq X$. Let $\theta=a/q+\beta$ with $(a, q)=1$, $\lvert \beta \rvert <1/q^2$ and $q<X$. Suppose ${\alpha}_1$ and ${\alpha}_2$ are two arithmetic functions supported in $[M, 2M]$ and $[N, 2N]$, respectively, and satisfy $|{\alpha}_1|, |{\alpha}_2| \leq \uptau_h\cdot \log $ for some fixed integer $h\geq 1$. Let $c$ and $d$ be non-zero positive integers such that $(c, d)=1$. Then, we have \begin{align} \bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{mn <X\\m\sim M, n\sim N\\mn\equiv c\imod d}}{\alpha}_1(m){\alpha}_2(n)e(mn\theta)\bigg\rvert\ll X\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X}+\dfrac{N}{X}+\dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2 + 2}, \end{align} where $H=1+|\beta|X$.
nodes.statement_short: Type II sum in a single progression mod $d$: $\ll X(M/X+N/X+qH/X+1/(qH))^{1/2}$ up to logs.
assumptions: ${\alpha}_1$ and ${\alpha}_2$ are two arithmetic functions supported in $[M, 2M]$ and $[N, 2N]$, respectively, and satisfy $|{\alpha}_1|, |{\alpha}_2| \leq \uptau_h\cdot \log $ for some fixed integer $h\geq 1$
$c$ and $d$ be non-zero positive integers such that $(c, d)=1$
nodes.label: lemmatypeIIpointwise

nodes.name: Equation (6.1)
nodes.statement: \bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{mn <X\\m\sim M, n\sim N\\mn\equiv c\imod d}}{\alpha}_1(m){\alpha}_2(n)e(mn\theta)\bigg\rvert\ll X\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X}+\dfrac{N}{X}+\dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2 + 2},
nodes.label: eq: pointwise

nodes.name: Proof of the point wise Type II estimate
nodes.statement: Let $\chi$ be Dirichlet character modulo $d$. Then, by the orthogonality of Dirichlet characters, we bound the sum in the left-hand side of \eqref{eq: pointwise} as \begin{align} \notag &\leq \dfrac{1}{\varphi(d)}\sum_{\chi\imod d}\bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{mn <X\\m\sim M, n\sim N}}{\alpha}_1(m)\chi(m){\alpha}_2(n)\chi(n)e(mn\theta)\bigg \rvert. \end{align} Now we use Lemma \ref{bilinear lemma} with ${\alpha}_1\cdot \chi$ and ${\alpha}_2\cdot \chi$ to estimate the sum over $mn <X$ and the trivial bound to sum over $\varphi(d)$ characters modulo $\chi$ to show that the above sum is \begin{align} &\ll X^{1/2}\lVert{\alpha}_1\rVert_2\lVert {\alpha}_2\rVert_2\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{N}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log qX). \end{align} Next, we recall that $|{\alpha}_1|, |{\alpha}_2|\leq \uptau_h \cdot \log $ to obtain \begin{align} \lVert{\alpha}_1\rVert_2\lVert{\alpha}_2\rVert_2 \leq \bigg(\sum_{m\sim M}\uptau_h(m)^2\bigg)^{1/2}\bigg(\sum_{n\sim N}\uptau_h(n)^2\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^2 \ll (MN)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2+1}, \end{align} using the fact that $\sum_{n< y}\uptau_h(n)^2 \ll y(\log y)^{h^2-1}$ for any real number $y\geq 2$. Substituting the estimate from \eqref{lemmapeq2} in \eqref{lemmapeq1} and using the fact that $MN\leq X$ and $q< X$ completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Detect the progression with Dirichlet characters and apply the bilinear estimate to each twisted sum.

nodes.name: Character orthogonality
nodes.statement: Let $\chi$ be Dirichlet character modulo $d$. Then, by the orthogonality of Dirichlet characters, we bound the sum in the left-hand side of \eqref{eq: pointwise} as \begin{align} \notag &\leq \dfrac{1}{\varphi(d)}\sum_{\chi\imod d}\bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{mn <X\\m\sim M, n\sim N}}{\alpha}_1(m)\chi(m){\alpha}_2(n)\chi(n)e(mn\theta)\bigg \rvert. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Detect $mn\equiv c$ by orthogonality of characters mod $d$.

nodes.name: Apply the bilinear estimate
nodes.statement: Now we use Lemma \ref{bilinear lemma} with ${\alpha}_1\cdot \chi$ and ${\alpha}_2\cdot \chi$ to estimate the sum over $mn <X$ and the trivial bound to sum over $\varphi(d)$ characters modulo $\chi$ to show that the above sum is \begin{align} &\ll X^{1/2}\lVert{\alpha}_1\rVert_2\lVert {\alpha}_2\rVert_2\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{N}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log qX). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 5.3 to each twisted sum.

nodes.name: Equation (6.2)
nodes.statement: &\ll X^{1/2}\lVert{\alpha}_1\rVert_2\lVert {\alpha}_2\rVert_2\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{N}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log qX).
nodes.label: lemmapeq1

nodes.name: Bound the $\ell^2$ norms
nodes.statement: Next, we recall that $|{\alpha}_1|, |{\alpha}_2|\leq \uptau_h \cdot \log $ to obtain \begin{align} \lVert{\alpha}_1\rVert_2\lVert{\alpha}_2\rVert_2 \leq \bigg(\sum_{m\sim M}\uptau_h(m)^2\bigg)^{1/2}\bigg(\sum_{n\sim N}\uptau_h(n)^2\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^2 \ll (MN)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2+1}, \end{align} using the fact that $\sum_{n< y}\uptau_h(n)^2 \ll y(\log y)^{h^2-1}$ for any real number $y\geq 2$. Substituting the estimate from \eqref{lemmapeq2} in \eqref{lemmapeq1} and using the fact that $MN\leq X$ and $q< X$ completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|\alpha_1\|_2\|\alpha_2\|_2$ via divisor moments and conclude.

nodes.name: Equation (6.3)
