nodes.statement: \lVert{\alpha}_1\rVert_2\lVert{\alpha}_2\rVert_2 \leq \bigg(\sum_{m\sim M}\uptau_h(m)^2\bigg)^{1/2}\bigg(\sum_{n\sim N}\uptau_h(n)^2\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^2 \ll (MN)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2+1},
nodes.label: lemmapeq2

nodes.name: Averaged Type II estimate over two moduli
nodes.statement: Let $c$ be a fixed non-zero integer. Let $D_1, D_2, M, N \geq 1$ be such that \[MN< X, \quad D_1M< X \quad \text{and} \quad D_1D_2^{2}N< X.\] Let $\theta=a/q+\beta$ with $(a, q)=1$, $\lvert \beta \rvert <1/q^2$ and $q<X$. Suppose ${\alpha}_1$ and ${\alpha}_2$ are two arithmetic functions with support $[M, 2M]$ and $[N, 2N]$, respectively, and satisfy $\lvert {\alpha}_1|, |{\alpha}_2| \leq \uptau_h\cdot \log $ for some fixed integer $h\geq 1$. Then, for any integer $h_1\geq 1$, we have \begin{align} \notag &\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{d_1\sim D_1\\d_2\sim D_2\\(cd_1,d_2)=1}}\uptau_{h_1}(d_1)\max_{(c', d_1)=1}\Bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{mn <X\\m\sim M, n\sim N\\mn\equiv c'\imod {d_1}\\mn\equiv c\imod {d_2}}}{\alpha}_1(m){\alpha}_2(n)e(mn\theta)\Bigg\rvert\\ \notag &\ll X\bigg(\dfrac{D_1M}{X} + \dfrac{(D_1D_2)^2}{X}+\dfrac{D_1D_2^2N}{X} + \dfrac{1}{D_1^{1/4}} + \dfrac{(qH)^{1/4}}{X^{1/4}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/4}}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2+h_1^2/2 + 5}, \end{align} where $H=1+|\beta|X$.
nodes.statement_short: Type II sums averaged over $d_1\sim D_1$, $d_2\sim D_2$ with a maximum over classes mod $d_1$; saves via averaging (Mikawa-Matomäki).
nodes.label: lemmatypeII

nodes.name: Proof of the averaged Type II estimate
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz over $m$, solve the congruences in $m$, reduce to sums of $\min(\cdot,\|d_1^2d''\theta\|^{-1})$. Matomäki's lemma with $\psi=1/4$ bounds the key sum.

nodes.name: Relation to prior proofs
nodes.statement: The proof of the lemma is closely related to the proofs of \cite[Proposition 9]{Mat} and \cite[Theorem (p.~352)]{Mik}, but for the convenience of the reader we include the proof here.
nodes.statement_short: The proof follows Matomäki and Mikawa.

nodes.name: Define $\mathcal{S}_{Type II}$
nodes.statement: We will estimate the sum: \begin{align}\notag \mathcal{S}_{\text{Type II}}:=\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{d_1\sim D_1\\d_2\sim D_2\\(cd_1,d_2)=1}}\uptau_{h_1}(d_1)\max_{(c', d_1)=1}&\Bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{mn <X\\m\sim M, n\sim N\\mn\equiv c'\imod {d_1}\\mn\equiv c\imod {d_2}}}{\alpha}_1(m){\alpha}_2(n)e(mn\theta)\Bigg\rvert. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Name the sum to bound.

nodes.name: Remove the maximum
nodes.statement: Let us assume that the maximum over $c'$ is attained at $c_{d_1}$. Let ${\lambda}(d_1, d_2)\in \mathbb{C}$ be of absolute value $1$ whenever $c'=c_{d_1}$ and $(d_1, c_{d_1})=(d_1, d_2)=(d_2, c)=1$ for $d_1\sim D_1$ and $d_2\sim D_2$. Then, we have \begin{align} \notag \mathcal{S}_{\text{Type II}}=\sum_{d_1\sim D_1}\uptau_{h_1}(d_1)\sum_{m\sim M}{\alpha}_1(m)\sum_{d_2\sim D_2}{\lambda}(d_1, d_2)\sum_{\substack{mn <X\\n\sim N\\mn\equiv c_{d_1}\imod {d_1}\\mn\equiv c\imod {d_2}}}{\alpha}_2(n)e(mn\theta). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Fix the maximising class and unimodular coefficients $\lambda(d_1,d_2)$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement:
We apply the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to obtain  egin{align} 
otag |\mathcal{S}_{	ext{Type II}}|^2\leq &~D_1 (\log X)^{h_1^2-1}\|{\alpha}_1\|_2^2\sum_{\substack{d_1\sim D_1}}\sum_{\substack{m\sim M}} igg|\sum_{\substack{d_2\sim D_2}}{\lambda}(d_1,d_2)\sum_{\substack{n<X/m\ n\sim N\ mn\equiv c_{d_1} \imod {d_1}\mn\equiv c\imod {d_2}}}{\alpha}_2(n)e(mn	heta) igg|^2\ 
otag \ll &~ D_1(\log X)^{h_1^2-1}\|{\alpha}_1\|_2^2\sum_{d_1\sim D_1}\sum_{\substack{d_2, d_2'\sim D_2\(d_2d_2', d_1)=1}}\sum_{\substack{n_1, n_2\sim N\(n_1, d_1d_2)=(n_2, d_1d_2')=1 }} ig|{\alpha}_2(n_1)\overline{{\alpha}_2(n_2)} ig|\ 
otag &	imes \Bigg|\sum_{\substack{m\sim M\m< \min (X/n_1, X/n_2)\mn_1\equiv mn_2\equiv c_{d_1}\imod {d_1}\mn_1\equiv c\imod {d_2}\mn_2\equiv c\imod {d_2'}}}e ig(m(n_1-n_2)	heta ig)\Bigg|\ 
otag \ll &~ D_1(\log X)^{h_1^2-1}\|{\alpha}_1\|_2^2\sum_{d_1\sim D_1}\sum_{\substack{d_2, d_2'\sim D_2\(d_2d_2', d_1)=1}}\sum_{j\in \{1, 2\}}\sum_{\substack{n_1, n_2\sim N\(n_1, d_1d_2)=(n_2, d_1d_2')=1 }} ig|{\alpha}_2(n_j)|^2\ 
otag &	imes \Bigg|\sum_{\substack{m\sim M\m< \min (X/n_1, X/n_2)\mn_1\equiv mn_2\equiv c_{d_1}\imod {d_1}\mn_1\equiv c\imod {d_2}\mn_2\equiv c\imod {d_2'}}}e ig(m(n_1-n_2)	heta ig)\Bigg| \end{align} using the fact $|{\alpha}_2(n_1)\overline{{\alpha}_2(n_2)}|\leq |{\alpha}_2(n_1)|^2 + |{\alpha}_2(n_2)|^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz over $d_1,m$ and expand the square.

nodes.name: Solve the congruences
nodes.statement: The above congruences $mn_1 \equiv mn_2 \equiv c_{d_1} \imod {d_1}$, $mn_1\equiv c \imod {d_2}$, and $mn_1\equiv c\imod {d_2'}$ have a solution in $m$ if and only if $(n_1, d_1d_2)=(n_2, d_1d_2')=1$ and $n_1 \equiv n_2\imod {d_1 (d_2, d_2')}$. Then, we have a unique solution $m\equiv h'\imod {d_1[d_2, d_2']}$ for some $h'\in \{0, 1, \dotsc, d_1[d_2, d_2']-1\} $. Next, we write \[n_1-n_2=n'd_1(d_2, d_2') \quad \text{and}\quad m=h'+ m'd_1[d_2, d_2']\] so that $|n'|< 4N/d_1(d_2, d_2')$ and $m'\ll 1+M/d_1[d_2, d_2']$. This implies that \begin{align} \notag m(n_1-n_2)=h'n'd_1(d_2, d_2') + d_1^2d_2d_2'n'm'. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Solve the congruences in $m$ and reparametrise.

nodes.name: Geometric sum bound
nodes.statement: Then, we have \begin{align} \notag \lvert\mathcal{S}_{\textup{Type II}}\rvert^2 \ll &~D_1(\log X)^{h_1^2-1}\lVert {\alpha}_1\rVert_2^2 \sum_{\substack{d_1\sim D_1}}\sum_{\substack{d_2, d_2^\prime \sim D_2\\(d_2d_2^\prime, d_1)=1}} \sum_{n_1\sim N}|{\alpha}_2(n_1)|^2\\\notag &\times \sum_{|n^\prime|< 4N/d_1(d_2, d_2^\prime)}\bigg|\sum_{m^\prime}e(m^\prime n^\prime d_1^2d_2d_2^\prime \theta)\bigg|\\ \notag \ll &~D_1(\log X)^{h_1^2-1}\lVert {\alpha}_1\rVert_2^2\lVert {\alpha}_2 \rVert_2^2\\ &\times \sum_{\substack{d_1\sim D_1}}\sum_{\substack{d_2, d_2^\prime \sim D_2\\(d_2d_2^\prime,d_1)=1}}\sum_{|n^\prime|< 4N/d_1(d_2, d_2^\prime)}\min\bigg(\dfrac{M}{d_1[d_2, d_2^\prime]}+1, \dfrac{1}{\|n^\prime d_1^2d_2d_2^\prime\theta\|}\bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the sum over $m'$ by a minimum.

nodes.name: Equation (6.4)
nodes.statement: \notag \lvert\mathcal{S}_{\textup{Type II}}\rvert^2 \ll &~D_1(\log X)^{h_1^2-1}\lVert {\alpha}_1\rVert_2^2 \sum_{\substack{d_1\sim D_1}}\sum_{\substack{d_2, d_2^\prime \sim D_2\\(d_2d_2^\prime, d_1)=1}} \sum_{n_1\sim N}|{\alpha}_2(n_1)|^2\\\notag &\times \sum_{|n^\prime|< 4N/d_1(d_2, d_2^\prime)}\bigg|\sum_{m^\prime}e(m^\prime n^\prime d_1^2d_2d_2^\prime \theta)\bigg|\\ \notag \ll &~D_1(\log X)^{h_1^2-1}\lVert {\alpha}_1\rVert_2^2\lVert {\alpha}_2 \rVert_2^2\\ &\times \sum_{\substack{d_1\sim D_1}}\sum_{\substack{d_2, d_2^\prime \sim D_2\\(d_2d_2^\prime,d_1)=1}}\sum_{|n^\prime|< 4N/d_1(d_2, d_2^\prime)}\min\bigg(\dfrac{M}{d_1[d_2, d_2^\prime]}+1, \dfrac{1}{\|n^\prime d_1^2d_2d_2^\prime\theta\|}\bigg).
nodes.label: meth2i

nodes.name: Diagonal terms
nodes.statement_short: Diagonal $n'=0$ contributes $D_1M+(D_1D_2)^2$.

nodes.name: Equation (6.5)
nodes.statement: \notag \lvert \mathcal{S}_{\textup{Type II}}\rvert^2\ll &~\lVert {\alpha}_1\rVert_2^2\lVert {\alpha}_2 \rVert_2^2(\log X)^{h_1^2-1} \bigg\{MD_1(\log X)^{3} + D_1^2D_2^2\\ & + D_1\sum_{\substack{d_1\sim D_1}}\sum_{\substack{d_2, d_2^\prime \sim D_2\\(d_2d_2^\prime,d_1)=1}}\sum_{1\leq |n^\prime| < 4N/d_1(d_2, d_2^\prime)}\min\bigg(\dfrac{M}{d_1[d_2, d_2^\prime]} + 1, \dfrac{1}{\lVert n^\prime d_1^2d_2d_2^\prime\theta\rVert}\bigg)\bigg\}.
nodes.label: meth2iii

nodes.name: Substitute $d''$
nodes.statement: Next, we write $n^\prime d_2d_2^\prime =d''$, so that \[0<|d''|=|n^\prime| d_2d_2^\prime = |n^\prime| (d_2,d_2^\prime)[d_2, d_2^\prime] < \dfrac{4D_2^2N}{D_1},\] since $0<|n^\prime| < 4N/d_1(d_2, d_2^\prime)$ and $d_1\sim D_1$. Moreover, \[\dfrac{M}{d_1[d_2, d_2^\prime]} = \dfrac{Md_1(d_2, d_2^\prime)|n^\prime|}{d_1^2 |n^\prime| d_2d_2^\prime} \ll \dfrac{MN}{d_1^2|d''|}.\] The above reduction yields \begin{align} \notag \lvert \mathcal{S}_{\textup{Type II}}\rvert^2\ll &~\|\alpha_1\|_2^2\|\alpha_2\|_2^2\bigg\{(D_1M+D_1^2D_2^2)(\log X)^{h_1^2+2}+ \\ & + D_1(\log X)^{h_1^2-1}\sum_{d_1\sim D_1}\sum_{1\leq |d''|\ll D_2^2N/D_1}\uptau_3(d'')\min\bigg(\dfrac{MN}{d_1^2|d''|} + 1,\dfrac{1}{\lVert d_1^2d''\theta\rVert}\bigg)\bigg\}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $d''=n'd_2d_2'$.

nodes.name: Equation (6.6)
nodes.statement: \notag \lvert \mathcal{S}_{\textup{Type II}}\rvert^2\ll &~\|\alpha_1\|_2^2\|\alpha_2\|_2^2\bigg\{(D_1M+D_1^2D_2^2)(\log X)^{h_1^2+2}+ \\ & + D_1(\log X)^{h_1^2-1}\sum_{d_1\sim D_1}\sum_{1\leq |d''|\ll D_2^2N/D_1}\uptau_3(d'')\min\bigg(\dfrac{MN}{d_1^2|d''|} + 1,\dfrac{1}{\lVert d_1^2d''\theta\rVert}\bigg)\bigg\}.
nodes.label: meth2ii

nodes.name: Trivial range
nodes.statement: We observe that if $D_2^2N/D_1\ll 1$, then we can bound the sum \[\sum_{d_1\sim D_1}\sum_{1\leq |d''|\ll D_2^2N/D_1}\uptau_3(d'')\min\bigg(\dfrac{MN}{d_1^2|d''|} + 1,\dfrac{1}{\lVert d_1^2d''\theta\rVert}\bigg) \ll \sum_{d_1\sim D_1}\bigg(\dfrac{MN}{d_1^2} + 1\bigg) \ll M + D_1. \] Therefore, we can assume that $D_2^2N/D_1\gg1$, otherwise the sum over $d''$ in \eqref{meth2ii} can be bounded trivially as above. Without loss of generality, we can assume that $d''>0$ in the above sum.
nodes.statement_short: The range $D_2^2N/D_1\ll1$ is trivial; assume $d''>0$.

nodes.name: Apply Matomäki's lemma
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 5.4 with $\psi=1/4$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, from the above estimate together with \eqref{meth2ii}, and recalling from \eqref{lemmapeq2} that $\lVert {\alpha}_1\rVert_2\lVert {\alpha}_2 \rVert_2 \ll X^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2+1}$, we obtain \begin{align} \notag \lvert \mathcal{S}_{\textup{Type II}}\rvert \ll &~ X^{1/2}\bigg(MD_1 + D_1^2D_2^2 + D_1D_2^2N+X\bigg(\dfrac{1}{D_1} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/4}\bigg)^{1/2}\\ \notag &\times (\log X)^{h^2+h_1^2/2+5}. \end{align} The above estimate on simplification completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the $\ell^2$ bounds.

nodes.name: Type II estimate averaged over one modulus
nodes.statement: Let $D, M, N\geq 1$ be such that \[DM<X, \quad N\leq M \quad \text{and} \quad MN<X.\] Let $\theta=a/q+\beta$ with $(a, q)=1$ and $|\beta|<1/q^2$. Suppose ${\alpha}_1$ and ${\alpha}_2$ are two arithmetic functions supported in $[M, 2M]$ and $[N, 2N]$, respectively, and satisfy $|{\alpha}_1|, |{\alpha}_2|\leq \uptau_h\cdot \log$ for some fixed integer $h\geq 1$. Furthermore, let $H=1+|\beta|X$ and $qH\in [1, X]$. Then for any integer $h_1\geq 1$, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{d\sim D}}\uptau_{h_1}(d)\cdot\max_{(c, d)=1}&\Bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{mn <X\\m\sim M, n\sim N\\mn\equiv c\imod d}}{\alpha}_1(m){\alpha}_2(n)e(mn\theta)\Bigg\rvert\\ \notag &\ll X\bigg(\dfrac{DM}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{X} + \dfrac{M^{1/9}}{X^{1/9}}+ \dfrac{(qH)^{1/9}}{X^{1/9}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/9}}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2+h_1^2/2 + 5}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Type II sums averaged over $d\sim D$ with maximum over classes: optimised combination of Lemmas 6.1 and 6.2 (Mikawa).
assumptions: $D, M, N\geq 1$ be such that \[DM<X, \quad N\leq M \quad \text{and} \quad MN<X.\]
nodes.label: Cor: D

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.3
nodes.statement:
Let $\Sigma_1$ be the sum we wish to estimate in the corollary. Then, by Lemma ef{lemmatypeIIpointwise} and the fact that $N\leq M$, we have  egin{align} \Sigma_1 &\ll DX igg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH} igg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2 + h_1+1}. \end{align} Next, we apply Lemma ef{lemmatypeII} with $D_1=D$ and $D_2=1$ along with the fact that $N\leq M$ to obtain  egin{align} \Sigma_1 \ll X igg(\dfrac{DM}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{X} + \dfrac{1}{D^{1/4}} + \dfrac{(qH)^{1/4}}{X^{1/4}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/4}} igg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2+h_1^2/2+5}. \end{align} From the inequalities \eqref{cor6.3a} and \eqref{cor6.3b}, we obtain  egin{align} \Sigma_1^2 \ll &~X^2 igg\{\dfrac{DM}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{X} +\dfrac{(qH)^{1/4}}{X^{1/4}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/4}} + \min igg(\dfrac{1}{D^{1/4}}, \dfrac{D^2M}{X} + \dfrac{D^2qH}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{qH} igg) igg\}\ 
otag &	imes (\log X)^{2h^2+h_1^2+10}. \end{align} Next, we have  egin{align} 
otag \min igg(\dfrac{1}{D^{1/4}}, \dfrac{D^2M}{X} + \dfrac{D^2qH}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{qH} igg) &\leq  igg(\dfrac{1}{D^{1/4}} igg)^{8/9}\cdot  igg(\dfrac{D^2M}{X} + \dfrac{D^2qH}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{qH} igg)^{1/9}\ 
otag &= igg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH} igg)^{1/9}. \end{align} Finally, we substitute the above estimate in \eqref{cor6.3c} along with the fact that $qH\in [1, X]$ to complete the proof of the corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Take the minimum of the pointwise bound (Lemma 6.1) and the averaged bound (Lemma 6.2 with $D_2=1$), interpolating with exponents $8/9,1/9$.

nodes.name: Pointwise bound
nodes.statement: Let $\Sigma_1$ be the sum we wish to estimate in the corollary. Then, by Lemma \ref{lemmatypeIIpointwise} and the fact that $N\leq M$, we have \begin{align} \Sigma_1 &\ll DX\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2 + h_1+1}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 6.1 to each modulus.

nodes.name: Equation (6.7)
nodes.statement: \Sigma_1 &\ll DX\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2 + h_1+1}.
nodes.label: cor6.3a

nodes.name: Averaged bound
nodes.statement: Next, we apply Lemma \ref{lemmatypeII} with $D_1=D$ and $D_2=1$ along with the fact that $N\leq M$ to obtain \begin{align} \Sigma_1 \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{DM}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{X} + \dfrac{1}{D^{1/4}} + \dfrac{(qH)^{1/4}}{X^{1/4}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/4}}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2+h_1^2/2+5}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 6.2 with $D_2=1$.

nodes.name: Combine the two bounds
nodes.statement: From the inequalities \eqref{cor6.3a} and \eqref{cor6.3b}, we obtain \begin{align} \Sigma_1^2 \ll &~X^2\bigg\{\dfrac{DM}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{X} +\dfrac{(qH)^{1/4}}{X^{1/4}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/4}} + \min\bigg(\dfrac{1}{D^{1/4}}, \dfrac{D^2M}{X} + \dfrac{D^2qH}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{qH}\bigg)\bigg\}\\ \notag &\times (\log X)^{2h^2+h_1^2+10}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Take the minimum of the two bounds.

nodes.name: Equation (6.9)
nodes.statement: \Sigma_1^2 \ll &~X^2\bigg\{\dfrac{DM}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{X} +\dfrac{(qH)^{1/4}}{X^{1/4}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/4}} + \min\bigg(\dfrac{1}{D^{1/4}}, \dfrac{D^2M}{X} + \dfrac{D^2qH}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{qH}\bigg)\bigg\}\\ \notag &\times (\log X)^{2h^2+h_1^2+10}.
nodes.label: cor6.3c

nodes.name: Optimise the minimum
nodes.statement: Next, we have \begin{align} \notag \min\bigg(\dfrac{1}{D^{1/4}}, \dfrac{D^2M}{X} + \dfrac{D^2qH}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{qH}\bigg) &\leq \bigg(\dfrac{1}{D^{1/4}}\bigg)^{8/9}\cdot \bigg(\dfrac{D^2M}{X} + \dfrac{D^2qH}{X} + \dfrac{D^2}{qH}\bigg)^{1/9}\\ \notag &=\bigg(\dfrac{M}{X} + \dfrac{qH}{X} + \dfrac{1}{qH}\bigg)^{1/9}. \end{align} Finally, we substitute the above estimate in \eqref{cor6.3c} along with the fact that $qH\in [1, X]$ to complete the proof of the corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Interpolate the minimum with exponents $8/9$ and $1/9$.

nodes.name: Type II estimate over composite moduli $d_1d_2$
nodes.statement_short: Type II sums over composite moduli $d_1d_2$ with fixed class: bounds under $D_1D_2^2N<X$ (a) or $D_1D_2^{3/2}<X^{1/2}$ (b).
assumptions: $D_1, D_2, M, N\geq 1$ be such that \[D_1M<X, \quad N\leq M, \quad \text{and} \quad MN<X.\]
nodes.label: Cor: D_1D_2ii

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.4
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemma 6.2 ($h_1=1$) and Corollary 6.3 ($D=D_1D_2$); optimise the minimum differently for parts (a) and (b).

nodes.name: Bound via Lemma 6.2
nodes.statement: We apply Lemma \ref{lemmatypeII} with $h_1=1$ and $c'=c$ to obtain \begin{align} \mathcal{S} \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{D_1M}{X} + \dfrac{(D_1D_2)^2}{X} + \dfrac{D_1D_2^2N}{X} + \dfrac{1}{D_1^{1/4}} + \dfrac{(qH)^{1/4}}{X^{1/4}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/4}}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2+6}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 6.2 with $c'=c$.

nodes.name: Bound via Corollary 6.3
nodes.statement: Next, we write $d=d_1d_2$, so that $d\in [D_1D_2, 4D_1D_2]$. We then apply Corollary \ref{Cor: D} with $D=D_1D_2$ and $h_1=2$ to obtain \begin{align} \mathcal{S} \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{D_1D_2M}{X} + \dfrac{(D_1D_2)^2}{X} + \dfrac{M^{1/9}}{X^{1/9}} + \dfrac{(qH)^{1/9}}{X^{1/9}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/9}}\bigg)^{1/2}(\log X)^{h^2+7}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Corollary 6.3 with $D=D_1D_2$.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: From the inequalities \eqref{cor6.4i} and \eqref{cor6.4ii}, we obtain \begin{align} \notag|\mathcal{S}|^2 \ll X^2\bigg\{\dfrac{D_1M}{X} + \dfrac{(D_1D_2)^2}{X}&+ \dfrac{M^{1/9}}{X^{1/9}} + \dfrac{(qH)^{1/9}}{X^{1/9}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/9}} \\ & + \min\bigg(\dfrac{D_1D_2^2N}{X} + \dfrac{1}{D_1^{1/4}}, \dfrac{D_1D_2M}{X}\bigg)\bigg\}(\log X)^{2h^2+14}, \end{align} where we have used the fact that $qH \in [1, X]$.
nodes.statement_short: Take the minimum of the two bounds.

nodes.name: Equation (6.12)
nodes.statement: \notag|\mathcal{S}|^2 \ll X^2\bigg\{\dfrac{D_1M}{X} + \dfrac{(D_1D_2)^2}{X}&+ \dfrac{M^{1/9}}{X^{1/9}} + \dfrac{(qH)^{1/9}}{X^{1/9}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{1/9}} \\ & + \min\bigg(\dfrac{D_1D_2^2N}{X} + \dfrac{1}{D_1^{1/4}}, \dfrac{D_1D_2M}{X}\bigg)\bigg\}(\log X)^{2h^2+14},
nodes.label: cor6.4iii

nodes.name: Part (a)
nodes.statement: Now we optimize the right-hand side of the above expression to obtain \begin{align}\notag \min\bigg(\dfrac{D_1D_2^2N}{X} + \dfrac{1}{D_1^{1/4}}, \dfrac{D_1D_2M}{X}\bigg) &\ll \dfrac{D_1D_2^2N}{X} + \bigg(\dfrac{1}{D_1^{1/4}}\bigg)^{4/5}\bigg(\dfrac{D_1D_2M}{X}\bigg)^{1/5}\\ \notag &\ll \dfrac{D_1D_2^2N}{X} + \dfrac{(D_2M)^{1/5}}{X^{1/5}}. \end{align} Substituting the above estimate in \eqref{cor6.4iii} completes the proof of the part (a) of the corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Optimise the minimum to prove part (a).

nodes.name: Part (b)
nodes.statement: Next, we note that \begin{align}\notag \min\bigg(\dfrac{D_1D_2^2N}{X} + \dfrac{1}{D_1^{1/4}}, \dfrac{D_1D_2M}{X}\bigg) &\ll \bigg(\dfrac{D_1D_2^2N}{X}\cdot \dfrac{D_1D_2M}{X}\bigg)^{1/2} + \bigg(\dfrac{1}{D_1^{1/4}}\bigg)^{4/5}\bigg(\dfrac{D_1D_2M}{X}\bigg)^{1/5}\\ \notag &\ll \dfrac{D_1D_2^{3/2}}{X^{1/2}} + \dfrac{(D_2M)^{1/5}}{X^{1/5}}. \end{align} The above estimate together with \eqref{cor6.4iii} completes the proof of part (b).
nodes.statement_short: A different interpolation proves part (b).

nodes.name: General exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.statement_short: If weighted Type I and Type II sums in progressions are small, so is the weighted exponential sum of $\Lambda$ (via Vaughan's identity).
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions
assumptions: $\sigma$ is an arithmetic function such that $\sigma$ is supported in $[1, D]$ with $D\leq X^{1/2-\delta}$, $|\sigma|\leq \uptau$
suppose that the following two conditions holds.
nodes.label: ExpGen

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.1
nodes.statement_short: Vaughan's identity with $U=X^{1/3}$ splits the sum into five pieces bounded trivially, by Type I (condition I) or by Type II (condition II).
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.name: Drop $(n,b)=1$
nodes.statement: We may drop the condition $(n, b)=1$ in the sum. Indeed, the contribution of $(n, b)>1$ is \begin{align}\notag \ll \bigg|\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c_d\imod d\\(n, b)>1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\bigg| & \ll D(\log D)(\log X)\uptau(b)\\ \notag & \ll_{b, \delta}X^{1/2-\delta}(\log X)^2 \ll_{b, \delta} X\cdot \dfrac{(qH)^{1/2+\delta}}{X^{1/2+\delta}}(\log X)^2, \end{align} which is negligible.
nodes.statement_short: The terms with $(n,b)>1$ are negligible.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.name: Define $\Sigma$
nodes.statement: Therefore, we can focus on bounding the following sum \begin{align} \Sigma:=\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c_d\imod d}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Name the sum $\Sigma$.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.name: Equation (7.1)
nodes.statement: \Sigma:=\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c_d\imod d}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta).
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.label: Gen Sigma

nodes.name: Vaughan's identity
nodes.statement_short: Decompose $\Lambda$ by Vaughan's identity into $\Sigma_1,\dots,\Sigma_5$.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.name: Equation (7.2)
nodes.statement: \notag \Sigma =& \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\sigma(d)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c_d\imod d}}\bigg(\Lambda_{\leq U}(n) + (\mu_{\leq U}*\log)(n) - (\mathfrak{f}_{\leq U}*1)(n)\\ \notag & - (\mathfrak{f}_{> U}*1)(n)+ (\mu_{>U}*\Lambda_{>U}*1)(n)\bigg)e(n\theta)\\ =&~\Sigma_1 + \Sigma_2 - \Sigma_3 - \Sigma_4 + \Sigma_5,
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.label: Gen Sigma i

nodes.name: Bound $\Sigma_1$
nodes.statement: Since $\Lambda \leq \log$, we can bound the sum $\Sigma_1$ as \begin{align} \Sigma_1 &\ll (\log X)\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\uptau(d)\bigg(\dfrac{X^{1/3}}{d} + 1\bigg)\ll (X^{1/3} + D)(\log X)^3 \ll X^{1/2} \ll \dfrac{X (qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\Sigma_1$ is bounded trivially.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.name: Equation (7.3)
nodes.statement: \Sigma_1 &\ll (\log X)\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\uptau(d)\bigg(\dfrac{X^{1/3}}{d} + 1\bigg)\ll (X^{1/3} + D)(\log X)^3 \ll X^{1/2} \ll \dfrac{X (qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}}.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.label: Gen Sigma ii

nodes.name: Bound $\Sigma_2,\Sigma_3$
nodes.statement: Next, we estimate the sums $\Sigma_2$ and $\Sigma_3$ using condition \ref{TypeI} with $\alpha_1\in \{\mu_{\leq X^{1/3}}, \mathfrak{f}_{\leq X^{1/3}}\}$ to obtain \begin{align} \Sigma_2, \Sigma_3 \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_1}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Type I condition handles $\Sigma_2,\Sigma_3$.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.name: Equation (7.4)
nodes.statement: \Sigma_2, \Sigma_3 \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_1}.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.label: Gen Sigma iii

nodes.name: Bound $\Sigma_4$
nodes.statement: Now we estimate the sum $\Sigma_4$ given by \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_4 = \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\sigma(d)\sum_{\substack{mn<X\\mn\equiv c_d\imod d\\ X^{1/3} \leq m\leq X^{2/3}}}\mathfrak{f}(m)e(mn\theta). \end{align} By a dyadic decomposition of summation ranges, we find that \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_4\ll (\log X)^3 \max_{1\leq D'\leq D}\max_{X^{1/3}\leq M\leq X^{2/3}}\max_{1\leq N\leq X^{2/3}}\bigg|\sum_{\substack{d\sim D'\\(d, b)=1}}\sigma(d)\sum_{\substack{mn<X\\mn\equiv c_d\imod d\\ m\sim M, n\sim N\\MN<X}}\mathfrak{f}(m)e(mn\theta)\bigg|. \end{align} Now we can apply condition \ref{Type II} with $\{\alpha_2, \alpha_3\}=\{\mathfrak{f}_{>X^{1/3}}, 1\}$ by considering whether $M$ or $N$ is longer or not. The key point is that both $M, N\leq X^{2/3}$. Therefore, we obtain \begin{align} \Sigma_4 \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_2+3}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Dyadic split and Type II condition handle $\Sigma_4$.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.name: Equation (7.5)
nodes.statement: \Sigma_4 \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_2+3}.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.label: Gen Sigma iv

nodes.name: Bound $\Sigma_5$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Similarly, by a dyadic decomposition of summation ranges in $\Sigma_5$, we have \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_5 \ll (\log X)^3 \max_{1\leq D'\leq D}\max_{X^{1/3}\leq M, N\leq X^{2/3}}\bigg|\sum_{\substack{d\sim D'\\(d, b)=1}}\sigma(d)\sum_{\substack{mn<X\\mn\equiv c_d\imod d\\ m\sim M, n\sim N\\MN<X}}\Lambda(m) (\mu_{> X^{1/3}}*1)(n)e(mn\theta)\bigg|. \end{align} Since both $M, N\in [X^{1/3}, X^{2/3}]$, without the loss of generality we can assume $N\leq M$ and apply condition \ref{Type II} with $\alpha_2=\Lambda_{>X^{1/3}}$ and $\alpha_3= \mu_{>X^{1/3}}*1$ to obtain \begin{align} \Sigma_5 \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_2+3}. \end{align} Hence, substituting the estimates from \eqref{Gen Sigma ii}, \eqref{Gen Sigma iii}, \eqref{Gen Sigma iv}, \eqref{Gen Sigma v} in \eqref{Gen Sigma i} completes the proof of the proposition.
nodes.statement_short: Type II condition handles $\Sigma_5$; combine all pieces.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.name: Equation (7.6)
nodes.statement: \Sigma_5 \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_2+3}.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.label: Gen Sigma v

nodes.name: Comparison of saving exponents
nodes.statement: Note that if $\delta>0$ small, $\delta_1\in \{\delta, \delta/2\}$, and $\delta_2, \delta_3\geq \delta_1$, then we have the following estimate \begin{align} \dfrac{1}{X^{\delta_1}} + \dfrac{1}{X^{\delta_2}} + \dfrac{(qH)^{\delta_3}}{X^{\delta_3}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta_3}} \ll \dfrac{(qH)^{\delta_1}}{X^{\delta_1}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta_1}}, \end{align} where $H=1+|\beta|X$ and $qH\in [1, X]$. We will use the above estimate in several occasions in the paper.
nodes.statement_short: Smaller saving exponents dominate: sums of $X^{-\delta_i}$ and $qH$ terms are bounded by the $\delta_1$ terms.
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.label: Delta Remark

nodes.name: Equation (7.7)
nodes.statement: \dfrac{1}{X^{\delta_1}} + \dfrac{1}{X^{\delta_2}} + \dfrac{(qH)^{\delta_3}}{X^{\delta_3}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta_3}} \ll \dfrac{(qH)^{\delta_1}}{X^{\delta_1}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta_1}},
nodes.section: 7.1 A general exponential sum estimate over primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.label: Delta remark eq 1

nodes.name: Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.statement: Let $\delta>0$, let $b$ be a fixed positive integer, and let $D\leq X^{1/3-\delta}$. Let $\theta= a/q + \beta$ with $(a, q)=1$ and $\lvert \beta\rvert <1/q^2$. Furthermore, let $H=1+|\beta|X$ and $qH\in [1, X]$. Then for some constant $C_1$, we have \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n \equiv c \imod d\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\bigg\rvert \ll_{b, \delta} X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_1}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bombieri-Vinogradov type exponential sum bound over primes for moduli $d\le X^{1/3-\delta}$ with a maximum over classes.
nodes.section: 7.2 Exponential sum estimates over primes in arithmetic progression
nodes.label: PropminorPrimeI

nodes.name: Equation (7.8)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n \equiv c \imod d\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\bigg\rvert \ll_{b, \delta} X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_1}.
nodes.section: 7.2 Exponential sum estimates over primes in arithmetic progression

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.2
nodes.statement_short: Linearise the maximum, apply Proposition 7.1; Type I by Lemma 5.5, Type II by Corollary 6.3, both with Remark 7.1.
nodes.section: 7.2 Exponential sum estimates over primes in arithmetic progression

nodes.name: Reduce to Proposition 7.1
nodes.statement: Without the loss of generality, we may assume that the maximum over $c$ is attained at $c_d$. Let $\lambda(d)\in \mathbb{C}$ be of absolute value $1$ whenever $c=c_d$ and $(d, bc_d)=1$ for $d\in [1, D]$, so that \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n \equiv c \imod d\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\bigg| = \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\lambda(d)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n \equiv c_d \imod d\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta). \end{align} We may now use Proposition \ref{ExpGen} with $\sigma =\lambda$ to establish the required bound. Note that $|\lambda|\leq 1$ in this case. So, it is enough to estimate the Type I and Type II sums.
nodes.statement_short: Linearise the max and reduce to the Type I/II conditions of Proposition 7.1.
nodes.section: 7.2 Exponential sum estimates over primes in arithmetic progression

nodes.name: Verify the Type I condition
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.5 with Remark 7.1 gives condition (I).
nodes.section: 7.2 Exponential sum estimates over primes in arithmetic progression

nodes.name: Verify the Type II condition
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 6.3 with Remark 7.1 gives condition (II).
nodes.section: 7.2 Exponential sum estimates over primes in arithmetic progression

nodes.name: Exponential sum over primes with composite moduli
nodes.statement: Let $\delta>0$ be small, and let $b$ be a fixed positive integer. Let $D_1\in [1, X^{1/3-\delta}]$ and $D_2\in [1, X^{1/9}]$. Let $\theta= a/q + \beta$ with $(a, q)=1$ and $|\beta|<1/q^2$. Furthermore, let $H=1+|\beta|X$ and $qH\in [1, X]$. Let $c$ be a fixed non-zero integer. Then for some constant $C_2>0$, we have \begin{align} \sum_{d_1\leq D_1}\sideset{}{^*}\sum_{\substack{d_2\leq D_2}}\bigg\lvert \sum_{\substack{n< X\\n \equiv c \imod {d_1d_2}\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\bigg\rvert \ll_{b, \delta} X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_2}, \end{align} where $*$ in the sum denotes the conditions $(d_1, d_2)=(d_1d_2, bc)=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential sum bound over primes in a fixed class for composite moduli $d_1d_2$, $d_1\le X^{1/3-\delta}$, $d_2\le X^{1/9}$.
nodes.section: 7.3 Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions with composite moduli
nodes.label: PropminorPrimeII

nodes.name: Equation (7.9)
nodes.statement: \sum_{d_1\leq D_1}\sideset{}{^*}\sum_{\substack{d_2\leq D_2}}\bigg\lvert \sum_{\substack{n< X\\n \equiv c \imod {d_1d_2}\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\bigg\rvert \ll_{b, \delta} X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_2},
nodes.section: 7.3 Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions with composite moduli

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.3
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 7.1 with $\sigma=\sum\lambda(d_1,d_2)$; Type II split by $M\le X^{1/2}$ (Corollary 6.3) or $M\ge X^{1/2}$ (Corollary 6.4(b)).
nodes.section: 7.3 Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions with composite moduli

nodes.name: Reduce to Proposition 7.1
nodes.statement: We write \begin{align} \notag \sum_{d_1\leq D_1}\sideset{}{^*}\sum_{\substack{d_2\leq D_2}}\bigg\lvert \sum_{\substack{n< X\\n \equiv c \imod {d_1d_2}\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\bigg\rvert =\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{d_1\leq D_1\\d_2\leq D_2}}\lambda(d_1, d_2)\sum_{\substack{n< X\\n \equiv c \imod {d_1d_2}\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta), \end{align} where $\lambda(d_1, d_2)$ is a complex number of absolute value $1$ whenever $( d_1d_2, bc)= (d_1, d_2)=1$ with $d_1\in [1, D_1]$ and $d_2\in [1, D_2]$. We now apply Proposition \ref{ExpGen} with \[{\sigma}(d)=\sum_{\substack{d_1d_2=d\\d_j\leq D_j\forall j}}\lambda(d_1, d_2),\] to establish the proposition. Note that $|{\sigma}| \leq \uptau$ in this case. So, it is enough to estimate the Type I and Type II sums.
nodes.statement_short: Write with unimodular $\lambda(d_1,d_2)$ and apply Proposition 7.1.
nodes.section: 7.3 Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions with composite moduli

nodes.name: Type I sums
nodes.statement: We can use Lemma \ref{lemmatype1} to estimate the Type I sums, which is similar to the proof of Proposition \ref{PropminorPrimeI}, so that condition \ref{TypeI} holds in Proposition \ref{ExpGen}.
nodes.statement_short: Type I sums by Lemma 5.5.
nodes.section: 7.3 Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions with composite moduli

nodes.name: Type II sum
nodes.statement: For Type II sums, we need to estimate the following sum \begin{align} \notag \Sigma_{\text{Type II}}:=\max_{\substack{D_1', D_2', M, N}}\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{d_1\sim D_1'\\d_2\sim D_2'\\(d_1d_2, bc)=1\\(d_1,d_2)=1}}\bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{mn<X\\mn\equiv c\imod {d_1d_2}\\m\sim M, n\sim N}}{\alpha}_1(m){\alpha}_2(n)e(mn\theta)\bigg\rvert, \end{align} where $|{\alpha}_1|, |{\alpha}_2|\leq \uptau_2 \cdot \log$ and the maximum is taken over those $D_1', D_2', M, N$ that satisfy \begin{equation} D_1'\in [1, D_1], \quad D_2'\in [1, D_2], \quad M, N\leq X^{2/3}, \quad MN<X, \quad \text{and} \quad N\leq M. \end{equation} We divide our analysis of the above Type II sum into two cases:
nodes.statement_short: Set up the Type II sum and its parameter ranges.
nodes.section: 7.3 Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions with composite moduli

nodes.name: Equation (7.10)
nodes.statement: D_1'\in [1, D_1], \quad D_2'\in [1, D_2], \quad M, N\leq X^{2/3}, \quad MN<X, \quad \text{and} \quad N\leq M.
nodes.section: 7.3 Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions with composite moduli
nodes.label: prop2eq1

nodes.name: Case $M\le X^{1/2}$
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 6.3 with $D=D_1D_2\le X^{4/9-\delta}$.
nodes.section: 7.3 Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions with composite moduli

nodes.name: Case $M\ge X^{1/2}$
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 6.4(b) using $D_1D_2^{3/2}\le X^{1/2-\delta}$.
nodes.section: 7.3 Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions with composite moduli

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The above two cases complete our analysis of Type II sum estimates. Hence, this completes the proof of the proposition.
nodes.statement_short: Both cases give condition (II).
nodes.section: 7.3 Exponential sum over primes in arithmetic progressions with composite moduli

nodes.name: Well-factorable exponential sum estimate
nodes.statement: Let $\delta>0$ and let $b$ be a fixed positive integer. Let $c$ be a fixed non-zero integer and let $\xi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be a well-factorable function of level $D\in [1, X^{1/2-\delta}]$ with $|\xi|\leq 1$. Let $\theta= a/q + \beta$ for some $(a, q)=1$ and $\lvert \beta\rvert <1/q^2$. Furthermore, let $H=1+|\beta|X$ and $qH\in [1, X]$. Then for some constant $C_3>0$, we have \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,bc)=1}}\xi(d)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n \equiv c \imod d\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\ll_{b, \delta} X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_3}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Exponential sum bound over primes weighted by a well-factorable function of level $D\le X^{1/2-\delta}$.
nodes.section: 7.4 Exponential sum over primes with a well-factorable function
assumptions: $\xi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be a well-factorable function of level $D\in [1, X^{1/2-\delta}]$ with $|\xi|\leq 1$
nodes.label: expwellfac

nodes.name: Equation (7.11)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,bc)=1}}\xi(d)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n \equiv c \imod d\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\ll_{b, \delta} X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_3}.
nodes.section: 7.4 Exponential sum over primes with a well-factorable function

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.4
nodes.statement_short: Small level via Proposition 7.2; otherwise Proposition 7.1, with Type II split by $M\le X^{1/2}$ (Corollary 6.3) or a well-factorable split $D_1=D'X^{1/2}/M$ (Corollary 6.4(a)).
nodes.section: 7.4 Exponential sum over primes with a well-factorable function

nodes.name: Small level
nodes.statement: If $D\leq X^{1/3-\delta}$, we can apply Proposition \ref{PropminorPrimeI} and the fact that $|\xi|\leq 1$ to establish the required bound in the proposition with $C_3=C_1$. Therefore, we can assume that $D>X^{1/3-\delta}$ for the rest of the proof.
nodes.statement_short: If $D\le X^{1/3-\delta}$ use Proposition 7.2; assume $D>X^{1/3-\delta}$.
nodes.section: 7.4 Exponential sum over primes with a well-factorable function

nodes.name: Reduce to Type II sums
nodes.statement: We will use Proposition \ref{ExpGen} with ${\sigma}(d)=\xi(d)$ for $d\in (X^{1/3-\delta}, X^{1/2-\delta}]$. The calculations for the Type I sums are analogous to, as in the proof of Proposition \ref{PropminorPrimeI}. We can apply Lemma \ref{lemmatype1} to estimate the Type I sum, so that condition \ref{TypeI} holds in Proposition \ref{ExpGen}. The key difference is the estimate for the Type II sums. So, we will explain the Type II sum estimates in this case. In order to do that, we must estimate the following Type II sum: \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_{\text{well-fac,Type II}}:=\max_{\substack{D', M, N}}\bigg|\sum_{\substack{d\sim D'\\(d, bc)=1}}\xi(d)\sum_{\substack{mn<X\\mn\equiv c\imod {d_1d_2}\\m\sim M, n\sim N}}{\alpha}_1(m){\alpha}_2(n)e(mn\theta)\bigg|, \end{align} where $|{\alpha}_1|, |{\alpha}_2|\leq \uptau_2\cdot\log$ and the maximum is taken over those $D'$, $M$ and $N$ that satisfy \[D'\in (X^{1/3-\delta}, X^{1/2-\delta}], \quad M, N\leq X^{2/3},\quad N\leq M, \quad MN<X.\] As in the proof of Proposition \ref{PropminorPrimeII}, we divide the analysis of $\Sigma_{\text{well-fac, Type II}}$ into two cases:
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 7.1; Type I as before; set up the Type II sum.
nodes.section: 7.4 Exponential sum over primes with a well-factorable function

nodes.name: Case $M\le X^{1/2}$
nodes.statement: \paragraph{\it Case 1:} Suppose that $M\leq X^{1/2}$. We apply Corollary \ref{Cor: D} with $h=2$, $h_1=1$, and the fact that $|\xi|\leq 1$ to obtain \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_{\text{well-fac,Type II}} \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{10}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 6.3 bounds the Type II sum.
nodes.section: 7.4 Exponential sum over primes with a well-factorable function

nodes.name: Case $M\in[X^{1/2},X^{2/3}]$
nodes.statement_short: Factor $d=d_1d_2$ with $D_1=D'X^{1/2}/M$ and apply Corollary 6.4(a).
nodes.section: 7.4 Exponential sum over primes with a well-factorable function

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The above two cases cover the entire range for the Type II sums. Therefore, condition \ref{Type II} holds in Proposition \ref{ExpGen}. Hence, this completes the proof of the proposition.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (II) holds; Proposition 7.1 gives the result.
nodes.section: 7.4 Exponential sum over primes with a well-factorable function

nodes.name: Semi-linear sieve exponential sum estimate
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon>0$ be small and let $\delta\in (0, 10^{-3}]$. Let $b$ be a fixed positive integer. Let $\lambda_{\textup{sem}}^-$ be a lower bound semi-linear sieve weights of level $D\in [2, X^{\frac{3}{7}(1-4\delta)-\varepsilon}]$, as given in Lemma \ref{fundsemi} and Lemma \ref{wellfacsem}. Let $\theta= a/q + \beta$ with $(a, q)=1$ and $\lvert \beta\rvert <1/q^2$. Furthermore, let $H=1+|\beta|X$ and $qH\in [1, X]$. Then, for some constant $C_4>0$, we have \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,2b)=1}}\lambda_{\textup{sem}}^-(d)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n \equiv 1 \imod d\\ n\equiv 3\imod 8\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\ll_{b, \delta, \varepsilon} X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_4}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Exponential sum bound over primes $\equiv 3 \bmod 8$ in classes $1 \bmod d$, weighted by lower semi-linear sieve weights of level up to $X^{3(1-4\delta)/7-\varepsilon}$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve
assumptions: $\lambda_{\textup{sem}}^-$ be a lower bound semi-linear sieve weights of level $D\in [2, X^{\frac{3}{7}(1-4\delta)-\varepsilon}]$, as given in Lemma \ref{fundsemi} and Lemma \ref{wellfacsem}
nodes.label: expsemi

nodes.name: Equation (7.12)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,2b)=1}}\lambda_{\textup{sem}}^-(d)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n \equiv 1 \imod d\\ n\equiv 3\imod 8\\(n, b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta)\ll_{b, \delta, \varepsilon} X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta/2}}{X^{\delta/2}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^{\delta/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_4}.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve
nodes.label: expsemieqM

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.5
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 7.1 with $\sigma=\lambda^-_{sem}$; Type II split into cases, the hardest using the well-factorability of Lemma 3.4 and Lemma 6.2.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Small level
nodes.statement: If $D\leq X^{1/10}$, the estimate in \eqref{expsemieqM} follows from Proposition \ref{PropminorPrimeI}. So, we may assume throughout the proof that $D\geq X^{1/10}$.
nodes.statement_short: Small level follows from Proposition 7.2; assume $D\ge X^{1/10}$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Type I and Type II sums
nodes.statement: We now apply Proposition \ref{ExpGen} with ${\sigma}=\lambda_{\textup{sem}}^-$. In order to do that, we consider the following Type I and Type II sums: \begin{align} \notag \Sigma_{\textup{sem, Type I}}&:= \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, 2b)=1}}\lambda_{\textup{sem}}^-(d)\sum_{\substack{mn<X\\mn \equiv 1 \imod d\\mn\equiv 3\imod 8\\m\in [1, X^{1/3}]}}{\alpha}(m)\log^j(n)e(mn\theta),\\ \notag \Sigma_{\textup{sem, Type II}}&:= \max_{D', M, N}\bigg|\sum_{\substack{d\sim D'\\(d, 2b)=1}}\lambda_{\textup{sem}}^-(d)\sum_{\substack{mn<X\\mn \equiv 1 \imod d\\mn\equiv 3\imod 8\\m \sim M, n\sim N}}{\alpha}_1(m){\alpha}_2(n)e(mn\theta)\bigg|, \end{align} where $j\in \{0, 1\}$, $|{\alpha}|, |{\alpha}_1|, |{\alpha}_2|\leq \uptau_2\cdot \log$ and the maximum is over those $D', M, N$ that satisfy \begin{equation} D' \in [X^{1/10}, X^{\frac{3}{7}(1-4\delta)-\varepsilon}], \quad M, N\leq X^{2/3}, \quad N\leq M, \quad MN<X. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define the Type I and Type II sums and parameter ranges.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Equation (7.13)
nodes.statement: D' \in [X^{1/10}, X^{\frac{3}{7}(1-4\delta)-\varepsilon}], \quad M, N\leq X^{2/3}, \quad N\leq M, \quad MN<X.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve
nodes.label: semieq0

nodes.name: Type I sums
nodes.statement: First, we use Lemma \ref{lemmatype1} to estimate the type I sum with $h_1=2, h_2=1, h_3=1, M\leq X^{1/3}$ and $D\leq X^{3(1-4\delta)/7-\varepsilon}$ to obtain \begin{align} \notag \Sigma_{\textup{sem, Type I}} \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta}}{X^{\delta}} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^\delta}\bigg)(\log X)^6. \end{align} This implies that condition \ref{TypeI} holds in Proposition \ref{ExpGen}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.5 gives condition (I).
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Remove the condition mod 8
nodes.statement: Next, by orthogonality of the Dirichlet characters $\chi_8$ modulo $8$, we have \begin{align} \notag |\Sigma_{\textup{sem, Type II}}|\leq \max_{D', M, N}\bigg|\sum_{\substack{d\sim D'\\(d, 2b)=1}}\lambda_{\textup{sem}}^-(d)\sum_{\substack{mn<X\\mn \equiv c \imod d\\m\sim M, n\sim N}}{\alpha}_1(m)\chi_8(m){\alpha}_2(n)\chi_8(n)e(mn\theta)\bigg|. \end{align} Next, we divide our analysis of the sum $\Sigma_{ \textup{sem, Type II}}$ into two cases.
nodes.statement_short: Detect $mn\equiv3\bmod 8$ with characters mod 8.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Case $M\le X^{1/2}$
nodes.statement: \noindent{\it Case 1:} Suppose that $M\leq X^{1/2}$. In this case, we use Corollary \ref{Cor: D} with $D=D'$, $c=1$, $h=2$, $h_1=1$, and the facts that $|\lambda_{\textup{sem}}^-|\leq 1$ and $D'\leq X^{3/7} \leq X^{1/2-2\delta}$, to obtain \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_{ \textup{sem, Type II}} & \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^\delta}{X^\delta} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^\delta}\bigg)(\log X)^{10}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 6.3 with $D=D'$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Case $M\in[X^{1/2},X^{2/3}]$
nodes.statement_short: Two subcases according to the size of $D'$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Case 2 set-up
nodes.statement: \paragraph{\it Case 2:} Suppose that $M\in [X^{1/2}, X^{2/3}]$. The assumption on $M$ implies that $N\leq X^{1/2}$. We now consider two subcases.
nodes.statement_short: Here $N\le X^{1/2}$; consider two subcases.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Case 2(a): $D'\le X^{1-2\delta-\varepsilon^2}/M$
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 6.3 with Remark 7.1.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Case 2(b): $D'>X^{1-2\delta-\varepsilon^2}/M$
nodes.statement_short: Factor $d=d_1d_2$ via Lemma 3.4 and apply Lemma 6.2.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Equation (7.14)
nodes.statement: X^{1/10} \ll D_1 \leq \dfrac{X^{1-2\delta}}{M} \quad \text{and} \quad D_1D_2^2\leq \dfrac{X^{1-4\delta}}{D_0} \leq \dfrac{M}{X^{2\delta}}.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve
nodes.label: semieqn: i

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The above cases cover the entire range for the Type II sums. Noting that $\delta>\delta/2$, we see that condition \ref{Type II} holds in Proposition \ref{ExpGen}. Hence, this completes the proof of the proposition.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (II) holds; Proposition 7.1 gives the bound.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Case 2(b) works for any well-factorable sieve weights
nodes.statement: We note that our proof of Case 2(b) in Proposition \ref{expsemi} can be generalized to any well-factorable sieve weights of level $D$ as long as $D\leq X^{1/2-2\delta}$. The same idea will feature in the proof of Proposition \ref{explin}.
nodes.section: 7.5 Exponential sum over primes with semi-linear sieve

nodes.name: Linear sieve exponential sum estimate
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon>0$ be small and let $\delta\in (0, 10^{-3}]$. Let $b$ be a fixed positive integer. Let $\lambda_{\textup{lin}}^+$ be an upper bound linear sieve weights of level $D\in [2, X^{1/2-2\delta-\varepsilon}]$, as given in Lemma \ref{fundlin} and Lemma \ref{wellfacclin}. Let $L$ be a real number such that $L\in [X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}, X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}]$ and let $\mathfrak{h}$ be a bounded arithmetic real-valued function. Let $\theta= a/q + \beta$ with $(a, q)=1$ and $|\beta|<1/q^2$. Furthermore, let $H=1+|\beta|X$ and $qH\in [1, X]$. Then for some constant $C_5>0$, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,\: 2b)=1}}\lambda_{\textup{lin}}^+(d)\sum_{\substack{\ell\sim L\\(\ell,b)=1}}\mathfrak{h}(\ell)&\sum_{\substack{n<X/2\ell\\2\ell n+1\equiv 0\imod {d}\\ \ell n\equiv 1\imod 4\\(n,b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e\Big((2\ell n+1)\theta\Big)\\ \ll_{b, \delta, \varepsilon} & X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta}}{X^\delta} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^\delta}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_5}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Exponential sum bound over $\Lambda(n)e((2\ell n+1)\theta)$ in classes mod $d$, weighted by upper linear sieve weights of level up to $X^{1/2-2\delta-\varepsilon}$.
assumptions: $\lambda_{\textup{lin}}^+$ be an upper bound linear sieve weights of level $D\in [2, X^{1/2-2\delta-\varepsilon}]$, as given in Lemma \ref{fundlin} and Lemma \ref{wellfacclin}
$L$ be a real number such that $L\in [X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}, X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}]$
$\mathfrak{h}$ be a bounded arithmetic real-valued function
nodes.label: explin

nodes.name: Equation (7.15)
nodes.statement: \notag \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,\: 2b)=1}}\lambda_{\textup{lin}}^+(d)\sum_{\substack{\ell\sim L\\(\ell,b)=1}}\mathfrak{h}(\ell)&\sum_{\substack{n<X/2\ell\\2\ell n+1\equiv 0\imod {d}\\ \ell n\equiv 1\imod 4\\(n,b)=1}}\Lambda(n)e\Big((2\ell n+1)\theta\Big)\\ \ll_{b, \delta, \varepsilon} & X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^{\delta}}{X^\delta} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^\delta}\bigg)(\log X)^{C_5}.
nodes.label: linearexpestimate

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.6
nodes.statement_short: As for Proposition 7.5: dyadic split, characters mod 4, then three cases by $D'$ and $M'$, the hardest using Lemma 3.6 and Lemma 6.2.

nodes.name: Similar to Proposition 7.5
nodes.statement: Let $\Sigma_{\text{lin}}$ be the sum we wish to estimate. The proof is similar to the proof of Proposition \ref{expsemi}.
nodes.statement_short: The proof mirrors that of Proposition 7.5.

nodes.name: Support of $\mathfrak{h}$
nodes.statement: We note that $\mathfrak{h}(\ell)$ is supported on $[L, 2L)$ with $L\in [X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}, X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}]$. We can proceed in the same way as in the proof of Proposition \ref{expsemi}.
nodes.statement_short: Note the support of $\mathfrak{h}$.

nodes.name: Dyadic split in $n$
nodes.statement: We begin with a dyadic decomposition of the range of $n$ variable, say $n\sim N$ in the sum $\Sigma_{\text{lin}}$. Note that since $L\in [X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}, X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}]$ and $n<X/2\ell$, we have that $N\leq X^{2/3+ 2\delta + \varepsilon}$. Moreover, we also have that $L\leq X^{2/3+2\delta + \varepsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: Dyadic split gives $N\le X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}$.

nodes.name: Bilinear form
nodes.statement: We therefore define two new parameters $M'$ and $N'$, where \[M'=\max\{L, N\}, \quad N'=\min\{L, N\}, \quad \text{so that} \quad N'M'<X, \quad N', M'\leq X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}.\] We also perform a dyadic decomposition on the range of $d$ variable, say $d\sim D^\prime$, with $D^\prime \leq D$. Similarly to the proof of Proposition \ref{expsemi}, we introduce Dirichlet characters $\chi_4$ modulo $4$ to detect the congruence condition $\ell n\equiv 1\imod 4$. Therefore, we have \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_{\textup{lin}} \ll (\log X)^2\max_{D', M', N'}\bigg|\sum_{\substack{d\sim D^\prime\\(d, 2b)=1}}\lambda^+_{\textup{lin}}(d)\sum_{\substack{mn<X\\mn\equiv -1\imod d\\m\sim M', n\sim N'}}\alpha_1(m)\alpha_2(n)e(mn\theta)\bigg|, \end{align} where for $m\sim \{M', N'\}$, \[\{\alpha_1(m), \alpha_2(m)\}=\{\mathfrak{h}(m)\chi_4(m)\cdot 1_{(m, b)=1}, \Lambda(m/2)\chi_4(m/2)\cdot 1_{(m/2, b)=1, \: 2|m}\},\] and the maximum is over those $D', M', N'$ that satisfy \begin{align} D'\in [2, X^{1/2-2\delta-\varepsilon}], \quad M', N' \leq X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}, \quad N'\leq M', \quad M'N'<X. \end{align} Note that since $\mathfrak{h}$ is bounded and $\Lambda\leq \log$, we have $|\alpha_1|, |\alpha_2|\leq \log$. We also recall from Lemma \ref{fundlin} that $|\lambda_{\textup{lin}}^+|\leq 1$. Next, we divide our analysis of the above sum into three cases.
nodes.statement_short: Set $M'=\max(L,N)$, $N'=\min(L,N)$ and rewrite as a bilinear Type II sum.

nodes.name: Equation (7.16)
nodes.statement: D'\in [2, X^{1/2-2\delta-\varepsilon}], \quad M', N' \leq X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}, \quad N'\leq M', \quad M'N'<X.
nodes.label: prop 5: eq1

nodes.name: Case $D'\le X^{1/10}$
nodes.statement: \noindent{\it Case 1:} Suppose that $D'\leq X^{1/10}$. We can then apply Corollary \ref{Cor: D} with $D=D'$ and $h_1=h=1$ to obtain \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_{\textup{lin}} &\ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^\delta}{X^\delta} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^\delta}\bigg)(\log X)^9. \end{align} For the rest of the two cases, we can assume that $D'\geq X^{1/10}$.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 6.3.

nodes.name: Case $M'\le X^{1/2}$
nodes.statement: \noindent{\it Case 2:} Suppose that $M'\leq X^{1/2}$ and $D'\in [X^{1/10}, X^{1/2-2\delta-\varepsilon}]$. In this case, we may apply Corollary \ref{Cor: D} with $D=D'$, $c=-1$, $h=h_1=1$ to obtain \begin{align} \notag \Sigma_{\textup{lin}} & \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(qH)^\delta}{X^\delta} + \dfrac{1}{(qH)^\delta}\bigg)(\log X)^9. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 6.3.

nodes.name: Case $M'\ge X^{1/2}$
nodes.statement_short: Two subcases by the size of $D'$.

nodes.name: Case 3 set-up
nodes.statement: \noindent{\it Case 3:} Suppose that $M'\in [X^{1/2}, X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}]$. The assumption on $M'$ implies that $N'\leq X^{1/2}$. We now consider two subcases.
nodes.statement_short: Here $N'\le X^{1/2}$; two subcases.

nodes.name: Case 3(a)
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 6.3 with Remark 7.1.

nodes.name: Case 3(b)
nodes.statement_short: Factor $d=d_1d_2$ by well-factorability and apply Lemma 6.2.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The above three cases cover the entire range for the sum $\Sigma_{\textup{lin}}$ and hence, the proposition is established.
nodes.statement_short: All cases covered; the proposition follows.

nodes.name: General Theorem
nodes.statement_short: If $\mathfrak{f}$ has a mean value, is equidistributed in progressions mod $dq$ ($q|X$) and has small weighted exponential sums, then $\mathfrak{f}(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n+s)$ is equidistributed on average over $d\le D$.
assumptions: $b$ be an integer that is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$
$s$ be a positive integer such that $(r-s, b)=1$
$\mathfrak{f}$ be an arithmetic function supported on integers co-prime to $b$ and $|\mathfrak{f}|\ll \log $
assume that the following three conditions hold.
conclusions: \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\bigg(\sum_{\substack{n < X\\n\equiv c_d \imod d}}\mathfrak{f}(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n+s) - \dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\bigg) \ll\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A},
nodes.label: Thm G

nodes.name: Equation (8.1)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\bigg(\sum_{\substack{n < X\\n\equiv c_d \imod d}}\mathfrak{f}(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n+s) - \dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\bigg) \ll\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^A},

nodes.name: Justification of $\alpha_b<\omega/2$

nodes.statement: We will show that for any $A>0$, \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{d\leq X^{1/3-\delta} \\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c, d)=1}\bigg|\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c\imod d}}\Lambda(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)-\dfrac{1}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{n<X}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\bigg| \ll_{A, b, \delta} \dfrac{X^\zeta}{(\log X)^A}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (8.2)

nodes.name: Choice of parameters in Theorem 7
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we can assume that $\max{(c, d)=1}$ is attained at some reduced residue class $c_d$ modulo $d$. Then, in Theorem \ref{Thm G}, we take $\mathfrak{f}(n)=\Lambda(n)1_{(n, b)=1}$ for $n<X$, $D=X^{1/3-\delta}$, $s=0$ and ${\sigma}$ to be the corresponding sign of the expression inside the absolute value of the left-hand side of \eqref{abse} whenever $(d, bc_d)=1$. Clearly, $|{\sigma}|=1\leq \uptau$.

nodes.name: Condition (a)

nodes.name: Equation (8.4)

nodes.name: Condition (c)

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus, the estimate \eqref{genthmeq1} in Theorem \ref{Thm G} holds for $\Lambda(n)1_{(n, b)=1}$ for $n<X$. nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2

Note that $|{\sigma}|\leq \uptau$ in this case. We may now check three conditions of Theorem \ref{Thm G}. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item It is evident that by the Prime Number Theorem \cite[Chapter 18]{dav}, condition \ref{Cond 1} holds with $\lambda_{d}=1$ for any $d\in [1, X)$. \item Condition \ref{Cond 2} follows from the Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem \cite[Chapter 28]{dav} and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. \item Proposition \ref{PropminorPrimeII} implies condition \ref{Cond 3} with $\omega=\delta/2$ and $C'=C_2$. \end{enumerate} As noted above in the proof of Theorem \ref{Main Theorem}, we can remove the co-primality condition $(n, b)=1$ with an admissible error $\ll_{b, \delta} X^{{4/9-\delta}}(\log X)^2$. This establishes Theorem \ref{Main Theorem2}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6
nodes.statement: Finally, we apply Theorem \ref{Thm G} to deduce Theorem \ref{Hyp2} by taking\[\mathfrak{f}(n)=(\mathfrak{h}*\Lambda)(n/2)1_{\substack{(n, b)=1,\: n\equiv 2\imod 8}} \quad \text{for $n\in [1, X)$},\] where $\mathfrak{h}$ is supported on $[L, 2L]$ with $L\in [X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}, X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}]$. Furthermore, we take $s=1, c_d=-1, {\sigma}=\lambda_{\textup{lin}}^+$ and $D=X^{1/2-2\delta-\varepsilon}$ in Theorem \ref{Thm G}. Now we check three conditions of Theorem \ref{Thm G}. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item By the Prime Number Theorem in arithmetic progressions \cite[Chapters 20, 22]{dav}, condition \ref{Cond 1} holds with $\lambda_d=\sum_{\ell\sim L,\: (\ell, 2bd)=1}\mathfrak{h}(\ell)/\ell$ for any $d\in [1, X)$. Since $\mathfrak{h}$ is bounded, we have $|\lambda_d|\ll \log L\ll\log X$. \item Arguing as in the proof of Theorem \ref{Main Theorem}, condition \ref{Cond 2} follows from the Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem for the Dirichlet convolution and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. In particular, we apply \cite[Theorem 9.17]{opera} with $\alpha = \mathfrak{h}$ and $\beta=\Lambda$. Note that since $\mathfrak{h}$ is supported on $[L, 2L)$ with $L\in [X^{1/3-2\delta-\varepsilon}, X^{2/3+2\delta+\varepsilon}]$, for $\ell n<y$ we have that $n<y/L$. Moreover, by Siegel-Walfisz theorem, $\Lambda$ satisfies the Siegel-Walfisz condition, and if $y\in [X^{3/4}, X]$, then we have $\ell, n <y/(\log y)^B$ for some $B$ large. Therefore, the Bombieri-Vinogradov type estimate holds for the above function $(\mathfrak{h}*\Lambda)\big(n/2\big)1_{\substack{n\equiv 2\imod 8}}$ for $n\leq y$. The Bombieri-Vinogradov type estimate together with the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality implies condition \ref{Cond 2}. \item We can apply Proposition \ref{explin} to check condition \ref{Cond 3} with $\omega=\delta$ and $C'=C_5$ to complete the proof of Theorem \ref{Hyp2}. \end{enumerate} This completes the proof of Theorem \ref{Hyp2}.

nodes.name: Exponential sum $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}$
nodes.statement: By Fourier inversion (see relation \eqref{fourinv}), we have \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{n < X\\n\equiv c_d \imod d}}\mathfrak{f}(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n+s) = \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{0\leq t<X}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg), \end{align} where for any $(c, d)=(d, b)=1$ and for any real number $\theta\in [0, 1)$, \begin{align} \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}(\theta): = \sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c\imod d}}\mathfrak{f}(n)e(n\theta). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Fourier inversion expresses the twisted sum through $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}$ and $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}$, the exponential sum of $\mathfrak{f}$ over $n\equiv c \bmod d$.

nodes.name: Proof outline of Theorem 7
nodes.statement: The strategy to prove Theorem \ref{Thm G} roughly goes as follows: \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item As outline in Section \ref{Setup}, we dissect $t/X$ into so-called major arcs and minor arcs. \item The major arcs contribution is estimated in Proposition \ref{PropMajArc} by employing conditions \ref{Cond 1} and \ref{Cond 2} of Theorem \ref{Thm G}. \item The minor arcs contribution is estimated in Proposition \ref{PropMinorArc1} by using Lemma \ref{lemd2} (hybrid bound) and condition \ref{Cond 3} of Theorem \ref{Thm G}. \item Finally, in Section \ref{sec: proof of gen} we combine Proposition \ref{PropMajArc} (major arcs estimate) and Proposition \ref{PropMinorArc1} (minor arcs estimate) to deduce Theorem \ref{Thm G}.
nodes.statement_short: Circle method outline: major arcs via conditions (a),(b), minor arcs via the hybrid bound and condition (c).

nodes.name: $L^1$ bound
nodes.statement: There exists a constant $C_b \in [1/\log b, 1+3/\log b]$ such that \begin{align} \notag \sup_{\vartheta\in \mathbb{R}}\sum_{0\leq t <b^k}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{t}{b^k} + \vartheta\bigg)\bigg| \ll_{b} (C_b b \log b)^k. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\sup_\vartheta\sum_{t<b^k}|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(t/b^k+\vartheta)|\ll_b (C_b b\log b)^k$.
