nodes.origin_citation: Maynard 2022 (Primes and polynomials with restricted digits), Lemma 5.1
nodes.label: lemd1

nodes.name: Proof of the $L^1$ bound
nodes.statement: We write $n=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}n_jb^j$ with $n_0=r$, so that for any real number $\theta\in [0, 1)$, \begin{align} \widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(\theta)=e(r\theta)\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}\cap[0, b^{k-1})}(b\theta). \end{align} The above factorization allows us to express our sum as \begin{align}\notag \sup_{\vartheta\in \mathbb{R}}\sum_{0\leq t <b^k}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{b^k}+ \vartheta\bigg)\bigg| \leq b\cdot \sup_{\vartheta\in \mathbb{R}}\sum_{0\leq t <b^{k-1}}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{b^{k-1}} + b\vartheta\bigg)\bigg| \ll b(C_bb\log b)^{k-1} \ll_{b} (C_bb\log b)^k, \end{align} where we have used \cite[Lemma 5.1]{May2} with $b^k$ replace by $b^{k-1}$ to the sum over $t$.
nodes.statement_short: Factor $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}$ off the last digit and apply Maynard's Lemma 5.1 at level $b^{k-1}$.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function

nodes.name: Equation (9.2)
nodes.statement: \widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(\theta)=e(r\theta)\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}\cap[0, b^{k-1})}(b\theta).
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function
nodes.label: factorMay

nodes.name: Large-sieve type estimate
nodes.statement: Let $Q\geq 1$. Then, we have \begin{align} \sup_{\vartheta\in \mathbb{R}}\sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{\substack{0<a <q\\(a, q)=1}}\sup_{\lvert \varepsilon\rvert < 1/2Q^2}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{a}{q}+\varepsilon +\vartheta\bigg)\bigg| \ll_{b} (Q^2+b^k)(C_b \log b)^k, \end{align} where $C_b$ is the constant as in Lemma \ref{lemd1}.
nodes.statement_short: Large-sieve bound for $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}$ at well-spaced rationals $a/q$, $q\sim Q$: $\ll (Q^2+b^k)(C_b\log b)^k$.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function
nodes.origin_citation: Maynard 2022 (Primes and polynomials with restricted digits), Lemma 5.2
nodes.label: lemmlargsieve

nodes.name: Equation (9.3)
nodes.statement: \sup_{\vartheta\in \mathbb{R}}\sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{\substack{0<a <q\\(a, q)=1}}\sup_{\lvert \varepsilon\rvert < 1/2Q^2}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{a}{q}+\varepsilon +\vartheta\bigg)\bigg| \ll_{b} (Q^2+b^k)(C_b \log b)^k,
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function
nodes.label: largsieveeq

nodes.name: Proof of the large-sieve type estimate
nodes.statement_short: Gallagher-Sobolev inequality for well-spaced points, then the factorisation and Maynard's Lemma 5.2 argument.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function

nodes.name: Gallagher-Sobolev
nodes.statement: Note that $a/q+\varepsilon$ with $(a, q)=1, q\sim Q$ and $|\varepsilon|<1/2Q^2$ are well-spaced by $\gg 1/Q^2$ in the interval $[0, 1]$. Therefore, by the Gallagher-Sobolev type inequality (see \cite{gal}), we have \begin{align}\notag \sup_{\vartheta\in \mathbb{R}}\sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{\substack{0<a <q\\(a, q)=1}}\sup_{\lvert \varepsilon\rvert < 1/2Q^2}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{a}{q}+\varepsilon + \vartheta\bigg)\bigg| \ll Q^2\int_0^1 |\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(u)|\textup{d}u + \int_0^1 \bigg|\dfrac{\textup{d}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(u)}{\textup{d}u}\bigg|\textup{d}u. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Well-spacing and the Gallagher-Sobolev inequality.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function

nodes.name: Bound the integrals
nodes.statement: By the relation \eqref{factorMay} and arguing similarly as in the proof of \cite[Lemma 5.2]{May2}, we may estimate the above sum as \begin{align} \notag \sup_{\vartheta\in \mathbb{R}}\sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{\substack{0<a <q\\(a, q)=1}}\sup_{\lvert \varepsilon\rvert < 1/2Q^2}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{a}{q}+\varepsilon + \vartheta\bigg)\bigg|& \ll Q^2\int_{0}^1|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}\cap [0, b^{k-1})}(bu)|\textup{d}u + \int_0^1 \bigg|\dfrac{\textup{d}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}\cap [0, b^{k-1})}(bu)}{\textup{d}u}\bigg|\textup{d}u.\\ \notag &\ll_{b} (Q^2 + b^k)(C_b\log b)^k, \end{align} as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the integrals via the factorisation as in Maynard.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function

nodes.name: Hybrid estimate
nodes.statement: Let $Q, B \geq 1$. Then, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{\substack{1\leq a<q\\(a, q)=1}}\sum_{\substack{|\eta|<B\\b^k a/q + \eta \in \mathbb{Z}}}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{a}{q} + \frac{\eta}{b^k}\bigg)\bigg| \ll_{b} (b-1)^k(Q^2B)^{\alpha_b} + Q^2B(C_b\log b)^k, \end{align} where $C_b$ is the constant described in Lemma \ref{lemd1}, and \begin{align} \alpha_b = \dfrac{\log \bigg(C_b\dfrac{b\log b}{b-1}\bigg)}{\log b}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Hybrid bound for $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}$ summed over $a/q+\eta/b^k$: $\ll (b-1)^k(Q^2B)^{\alpha_b}+Q^2B(C_b\log b)^k$.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function
nodes.origin_citation: Maynard 2022 (Primes and polynomials with restricted digits), Lemma 5.3
nodes.label: lemd2

nodes.name: Equation (9.4)
nodes.statement: \alpha_b = \dfrac{\log \bigg(C_b\dfrac{b\log b}{b-1}\bigg)}{\log b}.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function
nodes.label: alphab

nodes.name: $\alpha_b\to0$ as $b\to\infty$
nodes.statement: We note that $\alpha_b$ tends to $0$ as $b\rightarrow \infty$. Therefore, $\alpha_b$ will be small if we take $b$ large enough, which is a crucial point in our entire Fourier analytic set-up.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function

nodes.name: Proof of the hybrid estimate
nodes.statement: The proof follows from the relation \eqref{factorMay} in combination with the arguments of \cite[Lemma 5.3]{May2}.
nodes.statement_short: Factorisation plus Maynard's Lemma 5.3 argument.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function

nodes.name: $L^\infty$ bound
nodes.statement: Let $q<b^{k/3}$ be of the form $q=q_1q_2$ with $(q_1, b)=1$ and $q_1\neq 1$, and let $|\varepsilon| < 1/2b^{2k/3}$. Then, for any integer $a$ with $(a, q)=1$, we have \begin{align} \notag \bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{a}{q}+\varepsilon\bigg)\bigg| \ll_{b} (b-1)^k\exp\bigg(-c_b\dfrac{k}{\log q}\bigg), \end{align} for some constant $c_b>0$ depending only on $b$.
nodes.statement_short: $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(a/q+\varepsilon)$ is small, $\ll (b-1)^k\exp(-c_bk/\log q)$, when $q$ has a factor coprime to $b$.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function
nodes.origin_citation: Maynard 2022 (Primes and polynomials with restricted digits), Lemma 5.4
assumptions: $q<b^{k/3}$ be of the form $q=q_1q_2$ with $(q_1, b)=1$ and $q_1\neq 1$
nodes.label: lemd3

nodes.name: Proof of the $L^\infty$ bound
nodes.statement: The proof follows from the relation \eqref{factorMay} in conjunction with the argument of \cite[Lemma 5.4]{May2}.
nodes.statement_short: Factorisation plus Maynard's Lemma 5.4 argument.
nodes.section: 9 Fourier estimates for the digit function

nodes.name: Major arcs estimate for Theorem 7
nodes.statement: Let $C\geq 1$ be a large real number. Assume the setting of Theorem \ref{Thm G} and recall that $s$ is a positive integer such that $(r-s, b)=1$. Then we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c, d)=1}\bigg\lvert\dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)-\dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n< X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\bigg| \ll\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{5C+5}}, \end{align} where $\mathfrak{M}$ is given by the relation \eqref{maj}, and the implicit constant in $\ll$ depends at most on $b$, $C$ and $\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: On the major arcs the Fourier expansion matches the expected main term up to $X^\zeta/(\log X)^{5C+5}$.
assumptions: Assume the setting of Theorem \ref{Thm G}
$s$ is a positive integer such that $(r-s, b)=1$
nodes.label: PropMajArc

nodes.name: Major arcs $\mathfrak{M}_1$ contribution
nodes.statement: Let $C\geq 1$, $D\in [1, X)$, and recall the set $\mathfrak{M}_1$ is given by \begin{align} \notag \mathfrak{M}_1 =&\bigg\{t \in [0, X)\cap \mathbb{Z}: \bigg\lvert\dfrac{t}{X}-\dfrac{a}{q}\bigg\rvert \leq \dfrac{(\log X)^C}{X}\, \text{for some}\, (a, q)=1, 1\leq a<q \leq (\log X)^C, q\nmid X\bigg\}. \end{align} Assume the setting of Theorem \ref{Thm G}. Then we have \begin{align} \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\bigg\lvert \sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}_1}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)\bigg\rvert \ll \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{5C+5}}, \end{align} where the implicit constant in $\ll$ depends at most on $b$, $C$ and $\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: The $\mathfrak{M}_1$ part ($q\nmid X$) is negligible by the $L^\infty$ bound.
assumptions: Assume the setting of Theorem \ref{Thm G}.
nodes.label: Majorarc1

nodes.name: Equation (10.1)
nodes.statement: \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\bigg\lvert \sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}_1}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)\bigg\rvert \ll \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{5C+5}},
nodes.label: Majorarceq1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 10.2
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 9.4 makes $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}$ small on $\mathfrak{M}_1$; $\mathfrak{M}_1$ is small and $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}$ is bounded trivially.

nodes.name: Apply the $L^\infty$ bound
nodes.statement: If $t\in \mathfrak{M}_1$, we use Lemma \ref{lemd3} to obtain \begin{align} \notag \bigg\lvert \widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\bigg\rvert \ll_{b, C} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{8C+7}}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 9.4 on $\mathfrak{M}_1$.

nodes.name: Count and conclude
nodes.statement: We note that the cardinality of the set $\mathfrak{M}_1$ is at most $\ll (\log X)^{3C}$. Therefore, by relation \eqref{Triv: for f}, \begin{align} \notag \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{d \leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\bigg\lvert \sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}_1}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)\bigg\rvert & \ll_{b, C} \dfrac{1}{X}\cdot (\log X)^{3C}\cdot \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{8C+7}}\cdot X(\log X)\cdot\sum_{d\leq D}\dfrac{1}{d}\\ \notag & \ll_{b, C} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{5C+5}}. \end{align} This completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Count $\mathfrak{M}_1$ and use the trivial bound for $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}$.

nodes.name: Major arcs $\mathfrak{M}_2$ contribution
nodes.statement: Let $C\geq 1$. Recall that the set $\mathfrak{M}_2$ is given by \begin{align} \notag \mathfrak{M}_2 =\bigg\{&t \in [0, X)\cap \mathbb{Z}: \dfrac{t}{X}=\dfrac{a}{q}+ \dfrac{\eta}{X}\: \text{for some}\, (a, q)=1, 0\leq a <q\leq (\log X)^C,\\ \notag & \: q\geq 1, q\vert X,\: 0<\lvert \eta \rvert \leq (\log X)^C\bigg\}. \end{align} Assume the setting of Theorem \ref{Thm G}. Then we have \begin{align} \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\bigg\lvert \sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}_2}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)\bigg\rvert \ll\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{5C+5}}, \end{align} where the implicit constant in $\ll$ depends at most on $b$, $C$ and $\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: The $\mathfrak{M}_2$ part ($q|X$, $\eta\ne0$) is negligible by equidistribution (condition (b)).
assumptions: Assume the setting of Theorem \ref{Thm G}.
nodes.label: Majorarc2

nodes.name: Equation (10.2)
nodes.statement: \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\bigg\lvert \sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}_2}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)\bigg\rvert \ll\dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{5C+5}},
nodes.label: Majorarceq2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 10.3
nodes.statement_short: Trivial bound for $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}$; split $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}$ by CRT into progressions mod $dq$, partial summation, then condition (b).

nodes.name: Expand over $q$, $a$, $\eta$
nodes.statement: We call the left-hand side of \eqref{Majorarceq2} as $\Sigma_{\textup{Major}}$ and simplify the sum as \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_{\textup{Major}} & \leq \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\sum_{\substack{q\leq (\log X)^C\\q|X}}\sum_{\substack{a=0\\(a,q)=1}}^q\sum_{0<|\eta|\leq (\log X)^C}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{a}{q}+\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg|. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the $\mathfrak{M}_2$ sum.

nodes.name: Trivial bound for $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}$
nodes.statement: In the right-hand side of the above expression, since $q|X$, we have that $\eta$ is an integer in this case. Next, we use the trivial bound $|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(a/q+\eta/X)|\leq X^{\zeta}$ in the above estimate to obtain \begin{align} \Sigma_{\textup{Major}} \leq \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{X}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\sum_{\substack{q\leq (\log X)^C\\q|X}}\sum_{\substack{a=0\\(a,q)=1}}^q\sum_{0<|\eta|\leq (\log X)^C}\bigg|\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg|. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Use $|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}|\le X^\zeta$.

nodes.name: Equation (10.3)
nodes.statement: \Sigma_{\textup{Major}} \leq \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{X}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\sum_{\substack{q\leq (\log X)^C\\q|X}}\sum_{\substack{a=0\\(a,q)=1}}^q\sum_{0<|\eta|\leq (\log X)^C}\bigg|\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg|.
nodes.label: inner0

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Therefore, in order to establish the lemma it is enough to show that \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_{\textup{Major}}':=\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\sum_{\substack{q\leq (\log X)^C\\q|X}}\sum_{\substack{a=0\\(a, q)=1}}^q\sum_{0<|\eta|\leq (\log X)^C}\bigg|\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg| \ll_{C}\dfrac{X}{(\log X)^{5C+5}}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to bounding $\Sigma'_{Major}$.

nodes.name: Split by residues mod $q$
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align} \notag \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)=\sum_{\substack{m=1}}^qe\bigg(\dfrac{-ma}{q}\bigg)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c\imod {d}\\ n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n)e\bigg(\dfrac{-n \eta }{X}\bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Split $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}$ by residues mod $q$.

nodes.name: Chinese Remainder Theorem
nodes.statement: We note that since $q|X = b^k$ and $(n, b)=1$ (as $\mathfrak{f}(n)$ is supported on integers $n$ such that $(n , b)=1$), the congruence $n\equiv m\imod q$ implies that we either have $(m, q)=1$ or the above sum is empty. Furthermore, since $(d, b)=1$ and $q|X=b^k$, we have $(d, q)=1$. Therefore, by the Chinese Remainder Theorem, the system of congruences \begin{align} \notag n\equiv c\imod d \quad \text{and}\quad n\equiv m\imod q \end{align} has a unique solution modulo $dq$. This allows us to write \begin{align} \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)=\sum_{\substack{m=1\\(m,q)=1}}^qe\bigg(\dfrac{-ma}{q}\bigg)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c \imod{d}\\n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n)e\bigg(\dfrac{-n \eta }{X}\bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Only reduced classes survive; CRT combines the moduli.

nodes.name: Equation (10.4)
nodes.statement: \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)=\sum_{\substack{m=1\\(m,q)=1}}^qe\bigg(\dfrac{-ma}{q}\bigg)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c \imod{d}\\n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n)e\bigg(\dfrac{-n \eta }{X}\bigg).
nodes.label: inner

nodes.name: Define $\Psi$ and $\Delta$
nodes.statement: Next, if $(c, d)=(m, q)=1$, then for any $y\geq 2$, we denote \begin{align} \notag \Psi_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m):=\sum_{\substack{n<y\\n\equiv c\imod {d}\\n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n). \end{align} For any $y\in [X^{3/4}, X]$, we denote \[\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m):=\Psi_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m)-\frac{ y\lambda_{d}}{\varphi(dq)}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Define partial sums $\Psi_\mathfrak{f}$ and discrepancies $\Delta_\mathfrak{f}$.

nodes.name: Partial summation
nodes.statement: Using partial summation and the inequality \eqref{Triv: for f}, we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c \imod{d}\\n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n)e\bigg(\dfrac{-n \eta }{X}\bigg)=& \int_{X^{3/4}}^X e\bigg(\dfrac{-y\eta}{X}\bigg)\text{d}\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m) + \dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\varphi(dq)}\int_{X^{3/4}}^X e\bigg(\dfrac{-y\eta}{X}\bigg)\text{d}y\\ \notag &+ O\bigg(\log X + \dfrac{X^{3/4}\log X}{dq}\bigg)\\ =& \int_{X^{3/4}}^X e\bigg(\dfrac{-y\eta}{X}\bigg)\text{d}\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m) + O\bigg(\dfrac{\lambda_{d}X^{3/4}}{\varphi(dq)} + \log X + \dfrac{X^{3/4}\log X}{dq}\bigg), \end{align} where we have used the fact that $\eta$ is an integer, so that $\int_{1}^X e(-y\eta/X)\text{d}y=O(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Partial summation isolates $\Delta_\mathfrak{f}$.

nodes.name: Equation (10.5)
nodes.statement: \notag \sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c \imod{d}\\n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n)e\bigg(\dfrac{-n \eta }{X}\bigg)=& \int_{X^{3/4}}^X e\bigg(\dfrac{-y\eta}{X}\bigg)\text{d}\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m) + \dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\varphi(dq)}\int_{X^{3/4}}^X e\bigg(\dfrac{-y\eta}{X}\bigg)\text{d}y\\ \notag &+ O\bigg(\log X + \dfrac{X^{3/4}\log X}{dq}\bigg)\\ =& \int_{X^{3/4}}^X e\bigg(\dfrac{-y\eta}{X}\bigg)\text{d}\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m) + O\bigg(\dfrac{\lambda_{d}X^{3/4}}{\varphi(dq)} + \log X + \dfrac{X^{3/4}\log X}{dq}\bigg),
nodes.label: inner01

nodes.name: Integration by parts
nodes.statement: Next, using integration by parts, we have \begin{align} \int_{X^{3/4}}^X e\bigg(\dfrac{-y\eta}{X}\bigg)\text{d}\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m) &\ll (1+|\eta|)\max_{X^{3/4}<y\leq X}|\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m)|. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate by parts.

nodes.name: Equation (10.6)
nodes.statement: \int_{X^{3/4}}^X e\bigg(\dfrac{-y\eta}{X}\bigg)\text{d}\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m) &\ll (1+|\eta|)\max_{X^{3/4}<y\leq X}|\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m)|.
nodes.label: inner02

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Using the estimate from \eqref{inner02} in \eqref{inner01} along with the facts that $|\eta| \leq (\log X)^C$ and that $\lambda_d\ll \log X$, we obtain \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c \imod{d}\\n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n)e\bigg(\dfrac{-n \eta }{X}\bigg) &\ll (\log X)^C\max_{X^{3/4}< y\leq X}\big|\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m)\big|+ \dfrac{X^{3/4} (\log X)^2}{dq}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the inner sums by $\max|\Delta_\mathfrak{f}|$.

nodes.name: Equation (10.7)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c \imod{d}\\n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n)e\bigg(\dfrac{-n \eta }{X}\bigg) &\ll (\log X)^C\max_{X^{3/4}< y\leq X}\big|\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m)\big|+ \dfrac{X^{3/4} (\log X)^2}{dq}.
nodes.label: inner03

nodes.name: Sum over parameters
nodes.statement: Therefore, using the inequalities \eqref{inner} and \eqref{inner03}, we have \begin{align} \notag \Sigma_{\textup{Major}}' :=&\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\sum_{\substack{q\leq (\log X)^C\\q|X}}\sum_{\substack{a=0\\(a,q)=1}}^q\sum_{0<|\eta|\leq (\log X)^C}\bigg|\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg|\\ \notag \ll &~(\log X)^{4C}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\sum_{\substack{q\leq (\log X)^C\\q|X}}\max_{(c, d)=1} \max_{(m, q)=1}\max_{X^{3/4}<y\leq X}|\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(y; d, c; q, m)| + X^{3/4}(\log X)^{3C+3}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Sum over $d,q,a,\eta$.

nodes.name: Apply condition (b)
nodes.statement: We can now apply \ref{Cond 2} with $A=9C+5$ to obtain \begin{align}\notag \Sigma_{\textup{Major}}' \ll (\log X)^{4C} \cdot \dfrac{X}{(\log X)^{9C+5}} + X^{3/4}(\log X)^{3C+3} \ll \dfrac{X}{(\log X)^{5C+5}}, \end{align} as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (b) with $A=9C+5$.

nodes.name: Major arcs $\mathfrak{M}_3$ contribution (main term)
nodes.statement: Let $C\geq 1$. Recall that the set $\mathfrak{M}_3$ is given by \begin{align} \notag \mathfrak{M}_3 =&\bigg\{t \in [0, X)\cap \mathbb{Z}: \dfrac{t}{X}=\dfrac{a}{q}\: \text{for some}~~(a, q)=1, 0\leq a <q\leq (\log X)^C, q\geq 1, \: q\lvert X\bigg\}. \end{align} Assume the setting of Theorem \ref{Thm G} and recall that $s$ is a positive integer such that $(r-s, b)=1$. Then, we have \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\bigg\lvert\dfrac{1}{X} \sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}_3}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)-\dfrac{ \lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n< X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\bigg\rvert \ll \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{5C+5}}, \end{align} where the implicit constant in $\ll$ depends at most on $b$, $C$ and $\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: The $\mathfrak{M}_3$ part ($t/X=a/q$, $q|X$) gives the main term $\frac{\lambda_d}{\varphi(d)}\frac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum 1_{\mathcal{A}_r}$.
assumptions: Assume the setting of Theorem \ref{Thm G}
$s$ is a positive integer such that $(r-s, b)=1$
nodes.label: Majorarc3

nodes.name: Equation (10.8)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\max_{(c,d)=1}\bigg\lvert\dfrac{1}{X} \sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}_3}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)-\dfrac{ \lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n< X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\bigg\rvert \ll \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{5C+5}},
nodes.label: majorarceqn3

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 10.4
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}(-a/q)$ via condition (b) and Ramanujan sums; $q|b$ makes $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(a/q)$ explicit, giving the main term.

nodes.name: Rewrite $\mathfrak{M}_3$
nodes.statement: We begin with the following observation that for $k$ large enough \[``q\leq (\log X)^C,\: q|X=b^k" \quad \text{is equivalent to} \quad ``q\leq (\log X)^C,\: \text{for every}\: p|q, \: \text{we have} \: p|b".\] Therefore, we have \begin{align} \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}_3}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)=\dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{q \leq (\log X)^C\\p|q\Rightarrow p|b}}\sum_{\substack{0\leq a<q\\(a,q)=1}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{a}{q}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-sa}{q}\bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the $\mathfrak{M}_3$ sum over $q$ with $p|q\Rightarrow p|b$.

nodes.name: Equation (10.9)
nodes.statement: \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}_3}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)=\dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{q \leq (\log X)^C\\p|q\Rightarrow p|b}}\sum_{\substack{0\leq a<q\\(a,q)=1}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{a}{q}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d,c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-sa}{q}\bigg).
nodes.label: Maintermeq0

nodes.name: Split $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}$
nodes.statement: If $(a, q)=1$, we have \begin{align} \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}\bigg)=\sum_{\substack{m=1}}^q e\bigg(\dfrac{-ma}{q}\bigg)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c\imod{d}\\ n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Split $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}(-a/q)$ by residues.

nodes.name: Equation (10.10)
nodes.statement: \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}\bigg)=\sum_{\substack{m=1}}^q e\bigg(\dfrac{-ma}{q}\bigg)\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c\imod{d}\\ n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n).
nodes.label: Maintermeq00

nodes.name: Define $\Delta_\mathfrak{f}(X;dq)$
nodes.statement: Arguing similarly as in Lemma \ref{Majorarc2}, we note that $(d, q)=(m, q)=1$. For brevity, let \begin{align} \Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(X; dq):=\max_{(c, d)=1}\max_{(m, q )=1}\Bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c\imod d\\n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n)-\dfrac{ \lambda_{d} X}{\varphi(dq)}\Bigg\rvert. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Define the discrepancy $\Delta_\mathfrak{f}(X;dq)$.

nodes.name: Equation (10.11)
nodes.statement: \Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(X; dq):=\max_{(c, d)=1}\max_{(m, q )=1}\Bigg\lvert\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c\imod d\\n\equiv m\imod q}}\mathfrak{f}(n)-\dfrac{ \lambda_{d} X}{\varphi(dq)}\Bigg\rvert.

nodes.name: Ramanujan sum
nodes.statement: Then, we have \begin{align} \notag \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}\bigg) &=\dfrac{\lambda_{d} X}{\varphi(dq)}\sum_{\substack{m=1\\(m,q)=1}}^q e\bigg(\dfrac{-ma}{q}\bigg)+O\Big(\varphi(q)\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(X;dq)\Big)\\ &=\dfrac{ \lambda_{d}\mu(q) X}{\varphi(dq)}+O\Big(\varphi(q)\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(X;dq)\Big), \end{align} where we have used we have the expression for the Ramanujan sum (see \cite[p. 149]{dav}): if $(a, q)=1$, then \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{m=1\\(m,q)=1}}^q e\bigg(\dfrac{-ma}{q}\bigg)=\mu(q). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the main term with the Ramanujan sum $\mu(q)$.

nodes.name: Equation (10.12)
nodes.statement: \notag \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}\bigg) &=\dfrac{\lambda_{d} X}{\varphi(dq)}\sum_{\substack{m=1\\(m,q)=1}}^q e\bigg(\dfrac{-ma}{q}\bigg)+O\Big(\varphi(q)\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(X;dq)\Big)\\ &=\dfrac{ \lambda_{d}\mu(q) X}{\varphi(dq)}+O\Big(\varphi(q)\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}(X;dq)\Big),
nodes.label: maintermeq1

nodes.name: Equation (10.13)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{m=1\\(m,q)=1}}^q e\bigg(\dfrac{-ma}{q}\bigg)=\mu(q).
nodes.label: Ramanujan

nodes.name: Error via condition (b)
nodes.statement: Note that $|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(a/q)| \leq X^{\zeta}$, so that the contribution of the big-Oh term from relation \eqref{maintermeq1} to the expression in \eqref{majorarceqn3} is \begin{align} \notag \ll \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{d \leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\sum_{\substack{q\leq (\log X)^C\\q|X}}\sum_{0\leq a <q}\bigg \lvert \widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{a}{q}\bigg)\bigg \rvert\varphi(q)\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}\Big(X; dq\Big)\ll &~\dfrac{X^{\zeta}(\log X)^{2C}}{X}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d,b)=1}}\sum_{\substack{q\leq (\log X)^C\\q|X}}\Delta_{\mathfrak{f}}\Big(X;dq\Big). \end{align} We apply condition \ref{Cond 2} with $A=7C+5$, so that the above sum is \begin{align} \notag & \ll_{b, C} \dfrac{X^{\zeta}(\log X)^{2C}}{X}\cdot \dfrac{X}{(\log X)^{7C+5}} \ll_{b, C} \dfrac{X^\zeta}{(\log X)^{5C+5}}, \end{align} which is admissible.
nodes.statement_short: The error is admissible by condition (b).

nodes.name: Remaining main-term identity
nodes.statement: We are therefore left with showing that \[\dfrac{\lambda_d}{X}\sum_{\substack{q \leq (\log X)^C\\p|q\Rightarrow p|b}}\sum_{\substack{0\leq a<q\\(a,q)=1}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{a}{q}\bigg)\dfrac{X\mu(q)}{\varphi(dq)}e\bigg(\dfrac{-sa}{q}\bigg) = \dfrac{\lambda_d}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n).\]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a main-term identity.

nodes.name: Squarefree $q|b$
nodes.statement: It is evident from the relation \eqref{maintermeq1} that $q$ is supported on square-free integers. Therefore, we have $q|b$ since for every prime $p|q$ implies $p|b$. Then, by the relation \eqref{Arfourier} and the fact that $q|b$, we have \begin{align} \widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{a}{q}\bigg) =e\bigg(\dfrac{ar}{q}\bigg)\sum_{\substack{n< X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $q$ is squarefree with $q|b$, so $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(a/q)$ is explicit.

nodes.name: Equation (10.14)
nodes.statement: \widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{a}{q}\bigg) =e\bigg(\dfrac{ar}{q}\bigg)\sum_{\substack{n< X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n).
nodes.label: maintermeq2

nodes.name: Evaluate the main term
nodes.statement:
We also note that $(d, q)=1$ as $(d, b)=1$ and $q|b$. Furthermore, since by our assumption $(r-s, b)=1$, we have $(r-s, q)=1$. Therefore, using \eqref{maintermeq1}, \eqref{Ramanujan}, and \eqref{maintermeq2} allows us to estimate the main term as  egin{align} 
otag \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{q \leq (\log X)^C\p|q\Rightarrow p|b}}\sum_{\substack{0\leq a<q\(a,q)=1}}&\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r} igg(\dfrac{a}{q} igg)\dfrac{\lambda_{d} X\mu(q)}{\varphi(dq)}e igg(\dfrac{-sa}{q} igg)\ 
otag &= \dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\sum_{\substack{q \leq (\log X)^C\p|q\Rightarrow p|b}}\sum_{\substack{0\leq a<q\(a,q)=1}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r} igg(\dfrac{a}{q} igg)\dfrac{\mu(q)}{\varphi(q)}e igg(\dfrac{-sa}{q} igg)\ 
otag &=\dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\sum_{\substack{q|b}}\sum_{\substack{0\leq a<q\(a,q)=1}}e igg(\dfrac{a(r-s)}{q} igg)\dfrac{\mu(q)}{\varphi(q)}\ 
otag &=\dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\sum_{q|b}\dfrac{\mu^2(q)}{\varphi(q)}= \dfrac{ \lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n<X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n) \end{align} as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the Ramanujan sums to get $b/\varphi(b)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 10.1
nodes.statement: We can now combine Lemma \ref{Majorarc1}, Lemma \ref{Majorarc2} and Lemma \ref{Majorarc3} along with the fact that $\mathfrak{M}=\mathfrak{M}_1\cup\mathfrak{M}_2\cup\mathfrak{M}_3$ (see the relation \eqref{maj}) to complete the proof of Proposition \ref{PropMajArc}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemmas 10.2-10.4 over $\mathfrak{M}=\mathfrak{M}_1\cup\mathfrak{M}_2\cup\mathfrak{M}_3$.

nodes.name: Minor arcs estimate for Theorem 7
nodes.statement: Let $Q, B\geq 1$ with $QB \ll X^{1/2}$. Assume the set-up of Theorem \ref{Thm G}. Then we have \begin{align} \notag \sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{\substack{a=1\\(a,q)=1}}^q\sum_{\substack{B< |\eta|+1\leq 2B\\X a/q+\eta \in \mathbb{Z}}}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{a}{q}+\frac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(-\bigg(\frac{a}{q}+\frac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg)\bigg|\\ \notag \ll X^{1+\zeta}\bigg(\dfrac{1}{(Q^2B)^{\omega/2-\alpha_b}} + \dfrac{X^{\alpha_b}}{X^{\omega/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C'}, \end{align} where $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}, \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}$, and $\alpha_b$ are given by \eqref{Arfourier}, \eqref{Fourf}, and \eqref{alphab}, respectively. Furthermore, $\omega$ and $C'$ are as in condition \ref{Cond 3} of Theorem \ref{Thm G}, and the implicit constant in $\ll$ depends at most on $b$, $\delta$, and $\omega$.
nodes.statement_short: Dyadic minor-arc pieces are bounded by combining condition (c) with the hybrid bound.
assumptions: Assume the set-up of Theorem \ref{Thm G}.
nodes.label: PropMinorArc1

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 11.1
nodes.statement_short: $L^\infty$ bound from condition (c) times the $L^1$-type hybrid bound of Lemma 9.3 (Maynard's Lemma 6.1 idea).

nodes.name: Set-up
nodes.statement: We use ideas of Maynard from the proof of \cite[Lemma 6.1]{May2}. For $X=b^k$, we have \begin{align} \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)=\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c_d\imod d}}\mathfrak{f}(n)e\bigg(-n\bigg(\dfrac{a}{q}+\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Write $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}$ at $a/q+\eta/X$.

nodes.name: Equation (11.1)
nodes.statement: \widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)=\sum_{\substack{n<X\\n\equiv c_d\imod d}}\mathfrak{f}(n)e\bigg(-n\bigg(\dfrac{a}{q}+\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg).

nodes.name: Condition (c)
nodes.statement: We use condition \ref{Cond 3} with $\theta=a/q+\beta$ where $\beta=\eta/X$. Hence, for $q\sim Q$ and $(1+|\eta|)\sim B$ with $B\geq 1$, we note that $q (1 + |\beta|X)\asymp QB$ to obtain \begin{align} \sup_{\substack{q\sim Q\\(a,q)=1\\ (|\eta|+1) \sim B}}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg) \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(QB)^{\omega}}{X^\omega}+\dfrac{1}{(QB)^{\omega}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C'}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Sup bound from condition (c).

nodes.name: Equation (11.2)
nodes.statement: \sup_{\substack{q\sim Q\\(a,q)=1\\ (|\eta|+1) \sim B}}\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg) \ll X\bigg(\dfrac{(QB)^{\omega}}{X^\omega}+\dfrac{1}{(QB)^{\omega}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C'}.
nodes.label: minor2

nodes.name: Hybrid bound
nodes.statement: By assumption $QB\ll X^{1/2}$, so that $Q^2B \ll X$. Therefore, Lemma \ref{lemd2} implies that \begin{align} \sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{\substack{1\leq a <q\\(a,q)=1}}\sum_{\substack{(|\eta|+1)\sim B\\X a/q + \eta \in \mathbb{Z}}}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{a}{q} + \frac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg| \ll X^{\zeta}(Q^2B)^{\alpha_b}, \end{align} assuming that $b$ is large enough, so that $\alpha_b < 1$ and $\alpha_b \rightarrow 0$ as $b \rightarrow \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 9.3 bounds the sum of $|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}|$.

nodes.name: Equation (11.3)
nodes.statement: \sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{\substack{1\leq a <q\\(a,q)=1}}\sum_{\substack{(|\eta|+1)\sim B\\X a/q + \eta \in \mathbb{Z}}}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{a}{q} + \frac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg| \ll X^{\zeta}(Q^2B)^{\alpha_b},
nodes.label: minor3

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Putting the estimates from \eqref{minor2} and \eqref{minor3} together, we have \begin{align} \notag &\sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{\substack{a=1\\(a,q)=1}}^q\sum_{\substack{(|\eta|+1)\sim B\\X a/q+\eta \in \mathbb{Z}}}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\frac{a}{q}+\frac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg|\\ \notag &\ll X^{1+\zeta}\bigg(\dfrac{(QB)^{\omega}(Q^2B)^{\alpha _b}}{X^\omega}+\dfrac{(Q^2B)^{\alpha_b}}{(QB)^{\omega}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C'}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Multiply the two bounds.

nodes.name: Simplify
nodes.statement: By assumption $QB\ll X^{1/2}$, and by the fact that $(QB)^{\omega}> (Q^2B)^{\omega/2}$ for $B> 1$, the above estimate is \begin{align} \notag \ll X^{1+\zeta}\bigg(\dfrac{X^{\alpha_b }}{X^{\omega/2}}+ \dfrac{1}{(Q^2B)^{\omega/2-\alpha_b}}\bigg)(\log X)^{C'}. \end{align} This establishes the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Simplify using $QB\ll X^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7
nodes.statement_short: Circle method: Fourier inversion, major arcs via Proposition 10.1 and Cauchy-Schwarz, minor arcs via Dirichlet approximation, dyadic split and Proposition 11.1.

nodes.name: Fourier inversion
nodes.statement: By Fourier inversion (relation \eqref{fourinv}), we have \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{n < X\\n\equiv c_d \imod d}}\mathfrak{f}(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n+s) = \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{0\leq t<X}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg), \end{align} where $\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}$ and $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}$ are given by \eqref{Arfourier} and \eqref{Fourf}, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Express the sum by Fourier inversion.

nodes.name: Equation (12.1)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{n < X\\n\equiv c_d \imod d}}\mathfrak{f}(n)1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n+s) = \dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{0\leq t<X}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg),
nodes.label: Thm7eq1

nodes.name: Dissection
nodes.statement: We consider the parameter $C>0$ to be chosen later. Then we dissect the fractions $t/X$ with $t\in [0, X)\cap \mathbb{Z}$ into two sets: major arcs $\mathfrak{M}$ and minor arcs $\mathfrak{m}$ (see Section \ref{Setup} for definition of these two sets).
nodes.statement_short: Split into major and minor arcs.

nodes.name: Major arcs
nodes.statement: We may now use Proposition \ref{PropMajArc} to estimate the major arcs $\mathfrak{M}$ contribution. We will show that \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}&{\sigma}(d)\bigg(\dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)-\dfrac{ \lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n< X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\bigg)\ll \dfrac{X^\zeta}{(\log X)^C}. \end{align} For brevity, let us denote \begin{align} \notag \mathcal{E}(d):=\dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)-\dfrac{ \lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n< X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n). \end{align} We note that \[\quad \#\mathfrak{M} \ll (\log X)^{3C},\quad \big|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}(t/X)\big| \ll X^\zeta,\quad \text{and}\quad \big|\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}(-t/X)\big| \ll X(\log X)/d\] so that trivially, we have \[|\mathcal{E}(d)| \ll \dfrac{X^\zeta(\log X)^{C+1}}{d}.\] Next, we apply the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and use the assumption that $|\sigma|\leq \uptau$ to obtain \begin{align} \notag \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\mathcal{E}(d) &\ll \bigg(X^\zeta(\log X)^{3C+1}\sum_{d\leq D}\dfrac{\uptau(d)^2}{d}\bigg)^{1/2}\bigg(\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}\big|\mathcal{E}(d)\big|\bigg)^{1/2} \ll \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^C}, \end{align} using Proposition \ref{PropMajArc}. This completes our analysis of the major arcs.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 10.1 and Cauchy-Schwarz bound the major arcs.

nodes.name: Equation (12.2)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}&{\sigma}(d)\bigg(\dfrac{1}{X}\sum_{\substack{0\leq t<X\\t\in \mathfrak{M}}}\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{t}{X}\bigg)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-t}{X}\bigg)e\bigg(\dfrac{-st}{X}\bigg)-\dfrac{ \lambda_{d}}{\varphi(d)}\dfrac{b}{\varphi(b)}\sum_{\substack{n< X}}1_{\mathcal{A}_r}(n)\bigg)\ll \dfrac{X^\zeta}{(\log X)^C}.
nodes.label: Thm7eq2

nodes.name: Minor arcs
nodes.statement: We now use Proposition \ref{PropMinorArc1} for the remaining cases, that is, the minor arcs. We apply Dirichlet's approximation theorem to find reduced fractions $a/q$ with $1\leq q\leq X^{1/2}$ such that \[ \bigg|\dfrac{t}{X}-\dfrac{a}{q}\bigg|\leq \dfrac{1}{qX^{1/2}}.\] Hence, we have \[\dfrac{t}{X}=\dfrac{a}{q} + \dfrac{\eta}{X},\] where $\max \{q, |\eta|\}\geq (\log X)^C$ and $q|\eta|\leq X^{1/2}$. Next, we perform a dyadic decomposition over $q\sim Q$ and $|\eta|+1\sim B$, so that $QB\ll X^{1/2}$. Also note that we have $\max\{Q, B\} \gg (\log X)^C$ in this case. Therefore, the contribution of minor arcs is \begin{align} \notag&\ll \dfrac{(\log X)^2}{X}\sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{\substack{a=1\\(a,q)=1}}^q\sum_{\substack{B<|\eta|+1\leq 2B\\X\frac{a}{q} + \eta \in \mathbb{Z}}}\bigg|\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{A}_r}\bigg(\dfrac{a}{q}+\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\sum_{\substack{d\leq D\\(d, b)=1}}{\sigma}(d)\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_{d, c_d}\bigg(\dfrac{-a}{q}-\dfrac{\eta}{X}\bigg)\bigg|\\ \notag &\ll X^{\zeta} \bigg(\dfrac{(\log X)^{C'}}{(\log X)^{C(\omega/2-\alpha_b)}} + \dfrac{X^{\alpha_b}(\log X)^{C'}}{X^{\omega/2}}\bigg)(\log X)^2\ll \dfrac{X^{\zeta}}{(\log X)^{A}}, \end{align} where we have chosen $C=(A + C' +2)/(\omega/2-\alpha_b)$. Note that $\alpha_b$ goes to $0$ as $b\rightarrow \infty$ (see the relation \eqref{alphab}). In particular, since the base $b$ is sufficiently large, we have $\omega/2> \alpha_b$. Along with \eqref{Thm7eq2}, this completes the proof of Theorem \ref{Thm G}.
nodes.statement_short: Dirichlet approximation, dyadic split and Proposition 11.1 bound the minor arcs.
